# The story: how neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai changed what we built

For the judges, and for us in a month. Each claim names the file or trace that shows it. Longer detail is in [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md) (architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning, result per tool); the product itself is in the [README](../README.md). This page is kept current with every change: `scripts/lint_evidence.py` warns when it, STATUS or the build log fall behind the code.

## The thread in one paragraph
Storybound is an agent that promises things to a child's parent and checks the promises before the child sees a page. The three tools are not decoration around that idea; they are how we found out whether the promises were kept. **neatlogs** made every promise a visible, quoted verdict and told us, from traces we did not write a test for, what was slow, what was wrong and what was merely noise. **Entire** made every change one intent with a checkpoint, found a bug in our own evidence builder, and now gates the next change with rules written from what went wrong. **cfo.ai** turned "what does a story cost" into a decision that went back into the product (the agent now chooses which pages to paint), and then told us, honestly, that video AI would sink the margin and that a real launch needs about 2,500 paying households.

## neatlogs: from traces to fixes
| What neatlogs showed | What we did | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One trace per story, one GUARDRAIL span per verdict with the quoted text and the pass/fail | The receipt for parents is built from the same verdicts; a judge can open any story's trace and see which promise held on which page | `evidence/traces/`, [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md) section 1 |
| Reading level broke on most first-pass pages | Told the writer the limit: pages over the limit fell from 42.9% to 1.8% | [HR-001](../evidence/hardening/HR-001.md), [HR-003](../evidence/hardening/HR-003.md) |
| Its own triage opened three cards, unasked | We verified each before fixing: one confirmed (the 87 s stall), one partly (a "hurts" false positive), one refuted (it read neatlogs's own redaction as app behaviour) | [TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../evidence/neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md), [HR-004](../evidence/hardening/HR-004.md), [HR-005](../evidence/hardening/HR-005.md) |
| Measured cost per story ($0.0199, about 20% above our token estimate) | Replaced the estimate in the cfo.ai model | change 275839, `evidence/neatlogs/20261010-2010-IST-measured-vs-estimated-cost.json` |
| A second pass through traces, detections, alerts and analytics (11 Oct) | Found two detections that had never fired, no alert able to notify anyone, the 87 s stall back in bursts, and an unreported "ignore all" false stop; fixed the stall (hedged retry), the false stop (tiered), and the quiz detection ([HR-011](../evidence/hardening/HR-011.md)); six alert rules exist and need their thresholds retuned | [neatlogs-incident-review.md](research/neatlogs-incident-review.md), `evidence/neatlogs/review-2/` |
| Two judge-family spans on the same page | The judge bias test and the cross-family agreement check ([HR-008](../evidence/hardening/HR-008.md), [HR-012](../evidence/hardening/HR-012.md)) | `scripts/judge_bias.py`, `scripts/judge_agreement.py` |

What we would say to the neatlogs team: the triage cards and the detections found real things, MCP reads were the fastest way to check a claim, and three gaps cost us time: trace-level regexes cannot see multi-line GUARDRAIL text, error text is missing from `get_trace_context`, and the CLI login lasts only an hour.

## Entire: one intent per checkpoint, and rules for the next change
| What Entire did | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 40+ checkpoints, each tied to a commit with one intent; `entire why` and `graph impact` before touching the safety words; graph diffs of the hardening changes | `evidence/entire/` |
| `entire review general` on the PR that documented the history rewrite found five things, one a real bug (the evidence builder printed the latest commit as "First commit") | [PR 1](https://github.com/hatif03/storybound/pull/1), `evidence/entire/20261011-1010-IST-review-general-pr1.txt` |
| `entire review general` on the branch that spread the model work across providers found eight issues, all fixed, including a missing fallback that would have turned a gateway outage into a failed story | `evidence/entire/20261011-1415-IST-review-general-pr2.txt`, [HR-011](../evidence/hardening/HR-011.md) |
| Trails and runners: trails 2 and 3, each backed by a branch and a PR (the cloud runners did not report on those two because "Auto build on push" was off; once it was on, trail 4's review runner reported with no blocking findings); the three tailored runners now say what a prompt or promise change must bring (a bumped prompt version, a hardening record, a regression table) and what a button that deletes a child's work must be (a hold, or undoable) | `.entire/runners/`, [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md) sections 2 and 5 |
| Brain: durable facts recorded for the next session (Veo only in `us-central1`; gateway budget and routes; small-hands rules; the eval gate; the neatlogs login limit; tuning versus holdout) | `entire brain recall` |
| Honest limits: work before 15:08 on 10 Oct has no checkpoint; two pasted keys reached the checkpoint refs and were scrubbed by an approved history rewrite | [history-rewrite/NOTE.md](../evidence/history-rewrite/NOTE.md) |

## cfo.ai: a business model that talks back to the code
| Question we asked | What the model said | What changed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Can we paint every page? | No: 42.8% margin at month 6 against our 60% bar; half the pages clears it (67.2%) | The product setting `pictures`, and then `auto`: the agent spends a $0.16 picture budget on the pages that matter ([HR-010](../evidence/hardening/HR-010.md)) |
| Does sampled verification save money? | Under half a point | We kept full verification: safety does not get cheaper |
| What if we used video AI? | Three of the cheapest clips take the margin from 67% to -70%; a clip on every page, -640% | Motion stays deterministic; video, if ever, is a priced add-on (about $2.25 per story for three Lite clips) ([BUSINESS.md](BUSINESS.md)) |
| What would a real launch cost? | About $7,300 a month and $23,500 once (assumed), about 2,500 paying households at $6.99, or a $20.72 price at 500 | A checklist of what a product needs beyond the code ([BUSINESS.md](BUSINESS.md)) |
| Where do the hackathon credits go? | n/a (the gateway holds $20 and a story costs two cents) | A measured split of work across Gemini, K2 and the gateway, and the credits used for evaluation, not as spend for its own sake ([CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md)) |

## The numbers that make the story checkable
- Same writer, 28 drawing-and-lesson pairs: **27 of 28** stories shipped a broken promise ungated or self-reviewing, **0 of 28** gated ([report](../evidence/reports/20261010-1505-IST-sweep-2-p2.md)).
- Held-out drawings the prompts were never tuned on: 10 of 10 shipped with no break ([HR-008](../evidence/hardening/HR-008.md)).
- A frozen set of 16 past failures: 12 resolved under load, all 16 resolved when re-run alone.
- A generated video clip was rejected by the clip oath for redrawing the child's bunny ([HR-009](../evidence/hardening/HR-009.md)); deterministic motion remains the default.
- A first picture at 70 s instead of 278 s ([HR-010](../evidence/hardening/HR-010.md)).

## What did not work, said plainly
A 40 s timeout (reverted); Claude Haiku as the writer (3 of 10 stories shipped a break), as the character-card reader (it saw an ice-cream cone where a child drew a carrot) and as the safety screen (23 of 26 fixtures); trace-level regex detections on multi-line verdicts (never fired); a cfo.ai nested layout (rebuilt); the first regression and reading-pace runs, which overlapped other jobs and are marked as such.

Yes, every item in that evaluation looks like that, and it's my fault.

**Why it looks empty:** I added whole story traces to the evaluation, not individual verdicts. The top-level span of a story trace (`create-storybook`) had no input or output recorded, so neatlogs shows `{}` and `null` with "173 steps". The questions are about verdicts, which live in the `verify:*` spans inside the trace. Right now you'd have to click "Open trace" and dig through the steps for each of the 19 items.

**Fixes:**
- **Future traces:** the top-level span now records the request (lesson, age, arm, picture setting, repair cap) and the result (outcome, the receipt line, counts, broken promises). The change is committed as `0bfeecc` and tests pass.
- **This evaluation:** I want to rebuild it so each item is one verdict span, with the promise, the quoted text and the judge's reason visible on the item itself. Your 4 submitted answers stay on record, since I'd only close the old evaluation.

The rebuild needs a new neatlogs sign-in, because the last one expired after an hour. **Please approve this one (valid 10 min):** https://app.neatlogs.com/oauth/device?user_code=AMV5-4YG4-5V66-ERGD

OUT = Path(r"D:\storybound\evidence\neatlogs\review-3")
ENV = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("NEATLOGS_")}


def run(args, body=None):
    p = subprocess.run([N, *args], input=json.dumps(body) if body is not None else None, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=120, env=ENV)
    return (p.stdout or p.stderr).strip()


def key():
    return ["--idempotency-key", str(uuid.uuid4())]


res = {}
res["create"] = run(["evals", "create", "--body-stdin", *key()], {
    "name": "Do you agree with this verdict?",
    "description": "Single verdicts of the story checker (the K2 judge), each with the promise, the page text and the verdict. Does a human agree? Measures human and judge agreement.",
    "type": "human", "traceSource": "existing", "sendFrequency": "manual", "reviewDuration": "7d"})
EV = json.loads(res["create"])["data"]["id"]
res["form"] = run(["evals", "form", "set", EV, "--body-stdin", *key()], {
    "name": "Do you agree with this verdict?",
    "questions": [
        {"answerType": "multiple_choice", "questionText": "This step is one verdict of the story checker. Read the input (the promise and the page text) and the output (pass, violation, the quoted words and the reason). Do you agree with the verdict?", "isRequired": True, "sortOrder": 0, "options": {"options": ["Agree", "Disagree", "Cannot tell"]}},
        {"answerType": "paragraph", "questionText": "If you disagree or cannot tell: why? (Leave empty if you agree.)", "isRequired": False, "sortOrder": 1, "placeholder": "e.g. the quoted words do not show the promise being broken"},
    ],
})
sample = json.loads((OUT / "eval_sample_spans.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

prev = run(["evals", "cohort", "preview", EV, "--request-stdin"], {"action": "add", "references": refs})
res["preview"] = prev
pj = json.loads(prev)["data"]
bad = {r["referenceIndex"] for r in pj.get("rejections", [])}
if bad:
    refs = [r for i, r in enumerate(refs) if i not in bad]
    pj = json.loads(run(["evals", "cohort", "preview", EV, "--request-stdin"], {"action": "add", "references": refs}))["data"]
res["add"] = run(["evals", "cohort", "add", EV, "--request-stdin", *key()], {"previewHash": pj["normalizedInputHash"], "references": refs})
res["launch"] = run(["evals", "launch", EV, "--assign-me", "--review-duration", "7d", *key()])
res["evaluation_id"] = EV
(OUT / "eval_spans_create_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(res, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
print({k: v[:300] for k, v in res.items()})

# HR-014: architecture and configuration experiments: which writer, judge and repair budget is best?

Date: 12 Oct 2026. Asked by the neatlogs team's note (try different configurations and architectures, and see whether ours is the best at what it does) and by our own dashboard, which showed few incidents.

## Trigger
Every earlier claim compared the agent with itself (gated against ungated). Nobody had asked whether a different writer, a second judge, no judge, or a different repair budget would do better on the same drawings.

## Method
Ten held-out stories per configuration (five drawings the prompts were never tuned on, lessons sharing and honesty, gated arm, age 6), all run through `scripts/run_experiments.py`, each a tagged sweep (`experiment` in neatlogs, `experiment` and the full configuration in every `evidence/ledger.jsonl` row). The baseline is `holdout-routes-default` (HR-012). Results: [20261012-comparison.md](../experiments/20261012-comparison.md), made by `scripts/compare_experiments.py`. A second tool, `scripts/sweep.py --audit`, re-judges every page of every shipped story with the K2 judge and counts the breaks that remain (`kind: audit` rows).

## Results
| Configuration | Stories shipped | Shipped with a known break | Repairs a story | Seconds (mean) | Estimated $ a story |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline (Gemini Flash writer, K2 judge, 2 repairs) | 10 of 10 | 1 | 2.4 | 158 | 0.024 |
| X1 writer: Gemini 3.1 Pro | 10 of 10 | 0 | 1.3 | 213 | 0.113 |
| X2 writer: Claude Sonnet 4.6, first run | 7 of 10 (3 errors, see HR-015) | 1 | 2.7 | 138 | 0.091 |
| X2b writer: Claude Sonnet 4.6, after the parser fix | 10 of 10 | 0 | 5.1 | 218 | 0.122 |
| X3 judge ensemble (K2 and Sonnet, the stricter verdict wins) | 10 of 10 | 0 | 3.6 | 241 | 0.138 |
| X4 no judge (deterministic checks only) | 10 of 10 | 1 | 1.1 | 49 | 0.020 |
| X5 no repairs (the checks only observe what breaks) | 4 clean, 6 with notes | 6 | 0.4 | 154 | 0.018 |
| X6 four repairs a page instead of two | 10 of 10 | 0 | 2.5 | 177 | 0.022 |

The audit (the same ten drawings and lessons, 80 pages each, every page re-judged after shipping):

| Configuration | Pages with a break the shipped story still carries | Stories with at least one |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A0 baseline | 16 of 80 | 6 of 10 |
| A5 no repairs | 37 of 80 | 7 of 10 |
| A4 no judge | 48 of 80 | 8 of 10 |

## What we conclude
- **The checks only keep promises if they can repair.** Observing without repairing shipped a known break in 6 of 10 stories (X5); the audit shows the same effect at page level. Detection is not the product, repair is.
- **The judge matters more than it looks.** Without it a story takes 49 s and ships; the audit says 48 of its 80 pages break a promise the run never saw. The "shipped a break" column of X4 (1) is the number the agent knows about, not the number that is true.
- **A better writer helps and costs a lot.** Gemini Pro needs about half the repairs (1.3 against 2.4) at 4.7 times the cost; Claude Sonnet needs more (5.1) at five times the cost, so on this task it is worse than Pro. The cheap writer plus repair reaches the same shipped result for a fifth of the price, so the default stays.
- **A second judge is safe and expensive:** no extra breaks shipped, 3.6 repairs a story, 5.7 times the cost. It is kept as an option (`STORYBOUND_JUDGE_ENSEMBLE`), not the default; it is also the failover for the K2 judge (HR-015).
- **Two repairs are close to enough, four are slightly better at no cost:** 10 of 10 clean at 2.5 repairs a story, against 9 of 10 at 2.4 in the baseline. The difference is one story, so this is a candidate for a default change, not a result; the default stays at two until it is repeated.

## Limits, said plainly
Ten stories per configuration, one run each, five drawings: a single story moves a percentage by ten points, and no confidence interval is claimed. The audit judge is the same K2 judge that gates, so the audit measures what the judge can see on a second look (and its own variation: 16 of 80 pages in the baseline were flagged on a re-judge after the gate passed them), not an independent human truth; the human check of the judge is the neatlogs evaluation in `evidence/neatlogs/review-3/`. Costs are estimates from measured tokens at list prices; the Sonnet and ensemble costs are priced at the dearest gateway rate.

## Regression fixture
`python scripts/run_experiments.py --only X6` (any name in the `EXPERIMENTS` table); `python scripts/compare_experiments.py --md evidence/experiments/<file>.md`.

# HR-015: failure drills, and the four things they broke

Date: 12 Oct 2026. Our dashboard had few incidents, so we made some on purpose: `src/storybound/chaos.py` injects a failure (a stall, an error code, an outage) into one service for a run (`STORYBOUND_CHAOS=service:kind:value:probability`), the runs are tagged `chaos` in neatlogs, and each row in `evidence/ledger.jsonl` carries the setting. Five stories per drill (`scripts/run_experiments.py`), results in [20261012-comparison.md](../experiments/20261012-comparison.md).

## The drills and what they showed
| Drill | Failure injected | Result | What it found |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 / C2 | Gemini stalls for 100 s on 15% of calls, hedged retry on / off | 5 of 5 shipped both ways; mean 244 s against 294 s (longest 471 s against 415 s) | The hedge saves about 50 s on average; five stories each is too few to call it more |
| C3 | Gemini returns 503 on 40% of calls | 4 shipped, **1 shown a refusal** | An outage of the safety screen was shown to the child as "your picture was refused" |
| C3b | the same, after the fix | 4 shipped, **1 generic error** | A 503 that outlasted its retries in the character reader escaped as "something went wrong" |
| C4 | K2 (the judge) is down | **0 of 5 shipped:** 3 stopped, 1 refused, 1 error | One judge is a single point of failure; no story could be checked, so none was shown |
| C4b | K2 down, after the failover | 5 of 5 shipped, checked by the judge from another family ($0.129 a story, 5 times the usual) | The receipt says the judge changed |
| C5 | the model gateway is down | 5 of 5 shipped | Routes fall back to Gemini; no harm |
| C6 | image model returns 429 on 80% of calls | 2 shipped, 1 shipped with notes, 12 pictures failed; the whole run took 23 minutes | The agent falls back to a second image model and ships text-only pages when pictures cannot be painted; slow when the image service is the one failing |
| C7 | K2 and the gateway judge are both down | 5 of 5 stopped at the try-again screen, nothing unchecked shown | The safe failure: no verdict, no story |

## The four things found, and the fixes
1. **A page-JSON mismatch from a stronger writer** (X2, HR-014): Claude Sonnet's repair call returned the two answers as a `choices` list; the parser wanted `correct` and `wrong`, and 3 of 10 stories ended in an error. Found in neatlogs by opening the error spans; `writer.normalise()` now accepts both shapes and the error names the keys it saw. After the fix: 10 of 10 (X2b). Test: `tests/test_pipeline.py`.
2. **A judge outage was a dead end** (C4): the agent had one judge. Now a K2 error fails over to a judge from another family (`models.judge_fallback`), the receipt records the fallback, and a run where every judge fails stops at the try-again screen (C7).
3. **A service outage looked like a refusal** (C3): a screen that could not run was reported as unsafe. It is now `screen_unavailable`, and the child sees "Pip is having trouble right now. Please try again in a minute." (error code `service_unavailable`, documented in `docs/API.md`), never a refusal.
4. **A model error that outlived its retries escaped as a generic error** (C3b): `execute()` now maps any such error to the same try-again screen. Test: `test_a_model_service_that_fails_after_its_retries_shows_the_try_again_screen`.

## Limits, said plainly
Five stories per drill; the drills were run before and after the fixes on the same five drawings, so the "after" rows are a re-test of the same cases, not a fresh sample. The stall drill's saving (about 50 s) is within the spread of the runs. C6's 23 minutes is a real weakness: with the image service failing, the child waits for pictures that may not come; the text pages are ready much earlier, and a hard time budget for pictures is not built.

## Regression fixture
`python scripts/run_experiments.py --only C3b,C4b,C7`; unit tests for each fix in `tests/test_pipeline.py` and `tests/test_judge.py`.

# Demo video script (one video, at most 3:00)

Written for: the builder, who records and edits the video last. About 410 spoken words (about 2:50 at a calm pace); the screens are listed beside each line so each tool is shown on architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result. Everything said here is backed by a file or trace in the repo; the pointer is in the right-hand column so nothing needs to be looked up while recording.

**The three things the video must show (the brief):** the problem the agent solves · how cfo.ai and Entire were part of the project · how neatlogs was used to find and resolve the incidents the agent ran into.

| Time | On screen | Say | Proof to have open |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00 to 0:20 | A child's crayon drawing of a bunny; the story's first page; a magnifier on one page with words painted into the picture | "A child draws a bunny and asks for a story about sharing. A story model will write one. But nobody checks it: a word painted into the picture, a scary line, a lesson that never shows up. For a four to eight year old, that is the whole risk." | `assets/test-drawings/`, `evidence/stories/` |
| 0:20 to 0:50 | The receipt screen: "28 promises checked, 1 page rewritten, all kept"; then a page failing a check and being rewritten | "Storybound is an agent that writes an oath for each drawing and lesson, checks every page against it before the child sees it, rewrites any page that breaks it, and hands the parent a receipt. On the same writer, 27 of 28 stories shipped a broken promise without the checks. With them, none of 28." | [report](../evidence/reports/20261010-1505-IST-sweep-2-p2.md), [HR-008](../evidence/hardening/HR-008.md) |
| 0:50 to 1:50 | neatlogs: one story trace, its GUARDRAIL spans with quotes; then the incident cards; then the three fixes side by side | **Architecture and implementation:** "Every story is one neatlogs trace, and every promise is one span with the quoted words and the verdict. **Runtime:** we also broke things on purpose, so there would be incidents to find. **Incident one:** a stronger writer, Claude Sonnet, failed three stories in ten. In the trace the error span showed it had answered in a different shape. We made the parser accept both. Ten of ten. **Incident two:** with the judge down, no story shipped. Zero of five. We added a judge from another family. Five of five, and when both are down the child sees a try-again screen, never an unchecked story. **Incident three:** neatlogs opened its own cards, one said our repair loop never ends. We checked: the cap holds. The traces were fragments, because our worker threads lost their parent span. We fixed the tracing, and all four pictures and every picture check now sit inside the one story trace." | `evidence/hardening/HR-015.md`, `HR-016.md`, `evidence/neatlogs/review-3/triage_actions.json`, traces `640b8a6d6ed6cce8941ddab55139ffba` (after) and `f238415f0de63afe58fcbf9a32ff4f2a` (before) |
| 1:50 to 2:05 | The experiment table (writers, judge, no judge, no repairs) and the audit numbers | **Result:** "We also asked whether a different design would beat ours. Without repairs, six of ten stories shipped a known break. Without the judge, 48 of 80 pages broke a promise nobody saw. A stronger writer halves the repairs at five times the cost, so the cheap writer plus repair stays." | `evidence/experiments/20261012-comparison.md`, [HR-014](../evidence/hardening/HR-014.md) |
| 2:05 to 2:30 | Entire: the checkpoint list, `entire why` on a line, the review findings, a trail with its runner passing | **Entire:** "Entire kept every change as one intent with a checkpoint, so each fix above maps to one commit. Its review caught a real bug in our own evidence builder, and a missing fallback that would have turned a gateway outage into a failed story. Its trail runners now say what a prompt change must bring: a version bump, a hardening record, a regression run." | `evidence/entire/`, [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md) section 2, [PR 1](https://github.com/hatif03/storybound/pull/1) |
| 2:30 to 2:52 | cfo.ai: the Main scenario, margin cells, Version history of the cost edit, the video AI scenario in red | **cfo.ai:** "cfo.ai turned 'what does a story cost' into a decision. Painting every page left a 43 percent margin; so the agent now spends a fixed picture budget on the pages that matter. We replaced its cost guess with the cost neatlogs measured. And it told us video AI would take the margin from 67 percent to minus 70, so motion stays a cheap, checked effect." | `evidence/cfo/`, [BUSINESS.md](BUSINESS.md), [HR-010](../evidence/hardening/HR-010.md) |
| 2:52 to 3:00 | The receipt again, the repo name | "Promises written, checked, repaired, and shown to a parent. Storybound." | n/a |

## Recording notes
- Show, do not tell, for the incidents: three screen captures, each under 15 s: the Sonnet error span (`evidence/neatlogs/review-2/` and the X2 traces in the ledger), the drill C4 stopped runs next to C4b shipped, and the story trace before and after the span fix (span counts 2 of 4 pictures, 0 picture checks, against 4 and 8).
- Every number is a small-sample result (ten stories per configuration, five per drill). Do not say "always" or "proven"; say what was measured. If time is short, cut the 1:50 to 2:05 block first.
- No real child's face, name, school or location on screen; use the fixture bunny. The sister's drawings stay in `_private/`.
- Name the tools on screen as you speak (a lower-third: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai) so a judge scoring "each tool covered on architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning, result" can tick the five.
- If the human evaluation of judge verdicts has finished by recording time, add one sentence in the neatlogs block with its agreement number from `evidence/neatlogs/review-3/`; if not, say nothing about it.
- After the video: put the link in `evidence/posts.md`, then the submission post (Mon 12 Oct, 19:00 to 23:55 IST).

# HR-016: pictures and judge calls were missing from the story's trace (the orphan traces)

Date: 12 Oct 2026. Found by the neatlogs "picture words" detection that never fired, by one-span traces on the dashboard, and by three neatlogs incident cards that read fragments as failures. First recorded as unresolved in [HR-011](HR-011.md).

## Trigger
In a diagnostic story with four painted pictures (trace `f238415f0de63afe58fcbf9a32ff4f2a`), two `illustrate` spans and every `verify:image_*` span were missing from the story's trace; the dashboard also showed hundreds of traces of a single span named `IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B`, and the detection on picture-words verdicts had nothing to see.

## Diagnosis
Hypotheses written first: (1) the spans were never created; (2) they were created in worker threads that had no trace context; (3) they were created with a parent span that had already ended, and neatlogs exports a span whose parent has ended as a trace of its own. Hypothesis 1 was refuted (the child spans exist, as separate traces); a minimal thread-pool test showed hypothesis 2 was not the whole story (threads attached fine while the parent was alive); hypothesis 3 fit: a node span (`node.settle`, `node.verify`) ends when the node returns, but a judge call or a picture started inside it keeps running. The incident cards confirmed the effect from the other side: the "infinite repair loop" card linked three-span fragments (`illustrate` with its model calls and no story around them), not a loop.

## Change
`Run.task_context()` (`src/storybound/pipeline.py`) gives worker threads a copy of the context captured inside the workflow span, so work that outlives its node is parented to the workflow, not to the node. It is used for early pictures, the picture pool, and the oath engine's asynchronous judge calls (`task_context` in `src/storybound/oath/engine.py`). The story's span also records a request and a result now (lesson, age, arm, picture setting, repair cap; outcome, receipt line, counts), so a reviewer who opens it in neatlogs sees input and output instead of `{}` and `null`. Tests: `test_worker_threads_run_in_the_workflow_context_not_the_node_that_started_them`. Commits `74349c9` and `0bfeecc`.

## Before and after
| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `illustrate` spans in a four-picture story's trace | 2 of 4 | 4 of 4 (trace `640b8a6d6ed6cce8941ddab55139ffba`, [span list](../traces/20261012-IST-span-list-640b8a6d6ed6cce8941ddab55139ffba.json)) |
| `verify:image_*` spans in the same story's trace | 0 | 8 (four pictures, two picture promises) |
| Single-span `IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B` traces per story | 8.8 (88 for the ten stories of X6), 8.3 (X1), 9.8 (C1) | **0** for three clean stories (`postfix-spans`: 3 stories, 3 traces); 0 for the five drill stories of C4b (K2 was down there, so only the failover judge was exercised) |
| neatlogs incident cards from fragments | three open (repair loop, `illustrate` latency, K2 prose) | all three checked, explained and resolved with notes (`evidence/neatlogs/review-3/triage_actions.json`) |
| Picture-words detection (`Picture has words painted in`) | could not see picture verdicts | the verdict spans exist; its pattern matches a violation verdict and not a pass (tested on the real span format); **no story in these runs had a picture with words, so it has not fired** |

Numbers from `scripts/count_fragment_traces.py` (windows from the ledger; saved in `evidence/neatlogs/review-3/fragment_traces_by_experiment.json`).

## Limits, said plainly
- The audit runs (`--audit`) re-judge pages outside any story, so their windows hold hundreds of one-span and two-span traces by design; those windows cannot be used for this measure and were not.
- The "after" sample is three stories and one drill. It shows the fragments are gone in these runs, not for every code path; a new background thread would bring the problem back.
- The detection is correct on the span format but unproven on a real violation; a picture with painted words would have to occur (the vision judge flagged none in these runs).
- The hypothesis about the neatlogs exporter is inferred from behaviour, not from its source.
- The neatlogs trace export endpoint returned `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` when we tried to save the "before" trace, so the "before" counts are from the diagnostic session's notes and the dashboard, not from a saved file.

## Regression fixture
`python -m pytest tests/test_pipeline.py -k worker_threads`; to re-measure, run `python scripts/run_story.py benign/bunny-bow-carrot --lesson sharing --media --pictures auto --name diag-spans` and count the spans of its trace (`neatlogs traces spans list <id> --all --max-items 600`).

# claude-code review

Request changes. The branch has no quiz or games change; it adds failure drills, experiment tooling, a judge failover and tracing-context fixes. The reasons are below, and the main one is the safety-screen change that stops refusing drawings it could not screen. I did not run the tests.

10 findings, most severe first:

1. `src/storybound/pipeline.py:198`: Every 'screen_unavailable' result becomes a soft 'try again' error, but safety.screen() raises that reason for any exception, not only outages.

   Failure scenario: In safety.py:79-84 a Gemini content-block on a disturbing drawing, a non-JSON or missing visual_risk answer, or a code bug all return reason_code 'screen_unavailable'. A drawing the screen could not clear now gets 'Pip is having trouble, try again in a minute' with outcome 'error' and no run.refused event. The child can resubmit the same image repeatedly, and the ledger and receipt record an outage instead of a refusal. The fix is to split the reason in safety.screen(): ClientError with retryable or 5xx status becomes 'screen_unavailable', while a block or unparseable answer stays a refusal.

2. `src/storybound/oath/judge.py:158`: The ensemble lets one judge's 'pass' override the other judge's 'verification_error' on safety commitments.

   Failure scenario: engine.gate() treats verification_error on a safety-class commitment as critical (fail closed). In ensemble_batch, if the second judge errors or returns an unverifiable verdict, `x.status == 'verification_error' and y.status != 'verification_error'` picks the other judge's pass. A safety check one judge could not run is therefore reported as passed, which contradicts the 'stricter verdict wins' claim in the docstring. The fix is to keep the verification_error for safety-class commitments, or only fall through to the other judge for non-safety ones.

3. `src/storybound/oath/judge.py:132`: _RANK has no entry for 'warning', so a 'warning' ties with 'pass' and the result depends on argument order.

   Failure scenario: Judge A returns pass and judge B returns warning. _RANK.get gives both 0, so `x if rank(x) >= rank(y)` picks A (pass) and drops B's warning, although the stricter verdict was meant to win. Add 'warning': 1 and shift the others up.

4. `src/storybound/oath/judge.py:82`: The failover has no memory that the primary judge is down, so every batch pays the primary's full retry time before falling over, and a fallback row is written per batch.

   Failure scenario: With the K2 judge down, each judge_batch call (one or more per page, per story) retries K2 to exhaustion before using claude-sonnet-4.6, which adds seconds per page. record_fallback also appends one entry per call, so the receipt shows dozens of identical 'judge' fallbacks. Cache a short-lived 'primary down' flag, or dedupe fallbacks per role.

5. `src/storybound/pipeline.py:406`: n_stop decides 'the checkers were down' from `all(v.status == 'verification_error')`, which also matches causes unrelated to an outage.

   Failure scenario: A deterministic verifier crash ('verifier crashed: ...') or a judge returning a violation without a verbatim quote yields verification_error on a safety commitment. If those are the only critical-gated verdicts, a page that may genuinely be unsafe ends as a friendly 'try again' error instead of the calm stop, and the ledger records an error. Distinguish a judge outage from the other verification_error causes, for example by a marker on the verdict, before choosing 'unavailable'.

6. `src/storybound/config.py:61`: max_repair_attempts, the judge ensemble and the chaos hook are read from environment variables in product code, so a stray value silently changes behaviour.

   Failure scenario: STORYBOUND_MAX_REPAIRS=0 left in .env turns off repairs for real children's stories. STORYBOUND_CHAOS in .env injects 503s and stalls into production calls. A non-integer value makes int() raise at import and breaks the whole app. The chaos module says 'never set in the product' but nothing enforces it. Gate these behind STORYBOUND_EXPERIMENT, or parse defensively and log loudly when they are active.

7. `src/storybound/agents/writer.py:33`: normalise() unwraps any single-key dict, so the error message reports the wrong keys.

   Failure scenario: A writer answer like {'correct': {...}} has one dict-valued key, so it is unwrapped to the inner {'text', 'feedback'}. assemble() then reports 'missing scenario; it had the keys [feedback, text]', which hides the real shape from whoever debugs it. Only unwrap when the lone key is a known wrapper ('page', 'scene'), as the docstring says, and print the keys of the original dict.

8. `scripts/sweep.py:43`: audit_story judges after execute() has finished, outside the workflow span, and outside any metered() context.

   Failure scenario: Audit judge calls create stand-alone guardrail spans that neatlogs exports as one-span fragment traces. These pollute the fragment-trace counts that HR-016 and count_fragment_traces.py report, and audit token cost is not metered. Run the audit inside the story's own trace and metered context, or tag the audit spans so they are excluded from the counts.

9. `scripts/sweep.py:59`: one() now always passes pictures='auto' and media=media_on, which changes the configuration of every existing sweep.

   Failure scenario: Earlier sweeps and baselines ran with the default pictures setting and media=False. Re-running them now takes the 'auto' picture-planning path, so a new run is not directly comparable with older ledger rows, and ledger rows use a different `pictures` value. Pass pictures='auto' only when --media is set.

10. `scripts/count_fragment_traces.py:41`: `lo, hi = win[n]` raises KeyError when an experiment name is not in the ledger, aborting the whole run.

    Failure scenario: Passing a misspelled name

"""Save every span of one neatlogs trace through the MCP (project key; no sign-in needed) and count what matters for HR-016.

  python scripts/save_trace_spans.py <trace_id> <out.json>

The trace export endpoint and the CLI sign-in are not needed. The MCP pages 50 spans at a time and may answer 429 for a minute under load.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import neatlogs_mcp as m  # noqa: E402


def fetch(trace_id: str) -> dict:
    spans: list[dict] = []
    off = 0
    meta: dict = {}
    while True:
        r = m.rpc("tools/call", {"name": "get_trace_context", "arguments": {"trace_id": trace_id, "offset": off}})
        text = "".join(c.get("text", "") for c in r.get("result", {}).get("content", []))
        try:
            j = json.loads(text)
        except ValueError:
            time.sleep(60)
            continue
        if "spans" not in j:
            time.sleep(60)
            continue
        meta = {k: v for k, v in j.items() if k != "spans"}
        spans += j["spans"]
        if j.get("next_offset") in (None, off) or len(spans) >= j.get("span_count", 0):
            return {**meta, "spans": spans}
        off = j["next_offset"]


def main() -> None:
    tid, out = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2])
    d = fetch(tid)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    names = [s["name"] for s in d["spans"]]
    c = collections.Counter(n.split(":")[0] + (":" + n.split(":")[1] if n.startswith("verify:image") else "") for n in names if n.startswith(("illustrate", "verify:image")))
    print(f"{len(names)} spans of {d.get('span_count')}; illustrate={sum(n == 'illustrate' for n in names)}; picture checks={sum(n.startswith('verify:image') for n in names)}; {dict(c)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Drill: the painter writes words into a picture. Does the vision judge catch it, is the picture painted again, and does neatlogs' detection fire?

  python scripts/drill_picture_words.py [--name picture-words-drill] [--pictures 2]

The first painting of the first page is replaced by a picture with words painted in (the fixture bunny with a big caption drawn over it, made here);
every other painting is the real painter. Tagged `chaos` in neatlogs. Expected: a `verify:image_no_text` span with status violation, a
`scene.repair` event ("picture did not pass; painting it once more"), a second picture that passes, and a hit on the detection
"Picture has words painted in". Costs about $0.05 (a few pictures and checks).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import io
import sys
import threading
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from storybound import tracing  # noqa: E402

tracing.init()

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont  # noqa: E402

from storybound import media, pipeline  # noqa: E402
from storybound.clients import images as real_images  # noqa: E402
from storybound.clients.usage import Result  # noqa: E402
from storybound.events import EventLog  # noqa: E402

FIXTURE = ROOT / "assets" / "test-drawings" / "benign" / "bunny-bow-carrot.png"


def picture_with_words(src: bytes) -> bytes:
    """The fixture picture with large captions painted across it: what a painter that writes words into a scene produces."""
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(src)).convert("RGB").resize((768, 768))
    dr = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    font = ImageFont.load_default(size=88)
    for y, text in ((40, "HAPPY BUNNY"), (330, "SHARE THE"), (620, "CARROT!")):
        dr.rectangle((20, y - 6, 748, y + 100), fill=(255, 255, 255))
        dr.text((40, y), text, fill=(200, 30, 30), font=font)
    out = io.BytesIO()
    im.save(out, "PNG")
    return out.getvalue()


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--name", default="picture-words-drill")
    ap.add_argument("--save", help="write the picture with words here (a PNG)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    src = FIXTURE.read_bytes()
    bad = picture_with_words(src)
    if a.save:
        Path(a.save).write_bytes(bad)
    calls = {"n": 0}
    lock = threading.Lock()
    original = real_images.illustrate

    def illustrate(prompt, *, reference=None):
        with lock:
            calls["n"] += 1
            first = calls["n"] == 1
        if first:
            return Result(value=bad, raw_text="image/png")
        return original(prompt, reference=reference)

    pipeline.images.illustrate = illustrate  # the first painting only; the repaint and every other page are real

    sid = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
    bus = EventLog()
    run = pipeline.Run(
        cfg=pipeline.RunConfig(lesson_id="sharing", media=True, run_dir=ROOT / "runs" / sid, fixture="benign/bunny-bow-carrot", ledger_name=a.name, pictures="auto"),
        drawing=media.prepare(src), bus=bus, story_id=sid,
    )  # fmt: skip
    pipeline.execute(run)
    evs = bus.all()
    repairs = [e["data"] for e in evs if e["type"] == "scene.repair" and "picture" in str(e["data"].get("because", ""))]
    pic = [v for v in run.verdicts if v.commitment == "image_no_text"]
    print("OUTCOME:", run.outcome, "| trace", run.trace_id)
    print("PICTURE-WORDS VERDICTS:", [(v.scope, v.attempt, v.status, v.judge_model) for v in pic])
    print("PICTURE REPAINTS:", repairs)
    print("PAINT CALLS:", calls["n"])
    tracing.flush()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.content:
# Recording guide: our app, neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai

Written for: the builder, who records the one demo video (at most 3:00, script in [DEMO-SCRIPT.md](DEMO-SCRIPT.md)). Four captures, each short; the script says which seconds of each to use.

**Who records what.** The app capture is already made by a script (below), so you only need to record the three dashboards. The dashboards are behind your own logins (neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai); a script should not sign in as you, so you record them with OBS (it is in your taskbar) or Windows Game Bar (`Win + Alt + R`).

**Before you press record (all captures)**
- 1920 x 1080, browser zoom 100%, dark or light but the same for all three dashboards; close the bookmarks bar and other tabs.
- Hide what must not show: your email address (neatlogs, cfo.ai, Entire account menus), API keys, the `.env` file, `_private/`, any child's name. Do not open settings pages with keys.
- Move the mouse slowly, and pause one second on each thing you want a viewer to read. Record each segment as its own clip; do not try to do it in one take.
- Rehearse the clicks once without recording.

---

## 1. Our app (made for you)
File: `evidence/demo/app-walkthrough.webm` (a real story, real models, no mock; about 12 minutes raw because the story is really made while the recording runs). Cut it to about 45 seconds for the video: speed up the waiting with a 10x speed ramp, keep these moments at normal speed.

What the recording shows, in order, and what to say:
| Moment | What is on screen | What to say |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Welcome, "Let's go" | The home screen | "A child draws their own hero." |
| Drawing | A bunny drawn with the mouse | "No photo upload needed; this is drawn on the screen." |
| Name, lesson | Pip picks a name; the lesson card "Sharing"; the grown-up promise box with "Nobody in the story is left out" | "A parent chooses the lesson and can add a promise of their own." |
| Making the first page | The waiting screen | "Behind this screen the agent wrote an oath and is checking each page against it." |
| Reading a page | A picture, the scene, two choices | "Every page was checked before the child sees it." |
| A wrong answer | The story line shown after a wrong choice | "A wrong answer teaches, never scolds." |
| The quiz and the picture-order game | Four questions; the order game | "The quiz questions are verified too; a question that fails a promise is dropped." |
| Grown-ups, the receipt tab | The sum gate, the receipt: promises checked, pages rewritten, "could not be fully kept" | **This is the most important frame.** "The parent gets a receipt: how many promises were checked, how many pages were rewritten, and which could not be kept." |
| Forget | The story deleted | "And a parent can make the app forget the story." |

To run it again (costs about $0.45): start the server (`.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn storybound.api:app --app-dir src --port 8000`), then `cd web; node scripts\e2e-real.mjs --no-video --pictures auto --dwell 4 --record ..\evidence\demo\app-walkthrough.webm`. Add `--pictures full` to paint every page. To drive it by hand: open http://127.0.0.1:8000, press "Let's go", draw with the mouse or a finger (a simple shape is fine), "Done!", pick a name, pick "Sharing", press "Yes!", then read and answer; the grown-ups area is the small button on the top corner (answer the multiplication to open it).

## 2. neatlogs dashboard (about 60 seconds in the video, the longest block)
Open https://app.neatlogs.com, project "Mohammad's project". Record these in order:
1. **Traces** list, filter workflow `create-storybook`. Open `640b8a6d6ed6cce8941ddab55139ffba` (a story after the tracing fix). Expand the tree: the `node.*` steps, then a `verify:...` GUARDRAIL span; click it and show the quoted text, the verdict, the judge model. Say: "every promise is one span with the words it relied on."
2. **Before and after the tracing fix.** Show the trace `f238415f0de63afe58fcbf9a32ff4f2a` (208 spans, two pictures) then `640b8a6d...` (225 spans, four pictures and eight picture checks). Use the span counts shown at the top of each trace. (If the dashboard has dropped the old trace, use [the saved span lists](../evidence/traces/) on screen instead.)
3. **Incidents** page: the three cards that opened on 12 Oct, each resolved with a note: "Resolve Infinite Repair Loop..." (our tracing fault, not a loop), "Investigate Latency and Quota Exhaustion in `illustrate`" (our own drill), "Enforce Structured JSON Outputs ... K2" (refuted by the span). Open the first one, scroll to its resolution note and its linked traces (the three-span fragments). Say what the incident feature did: it surfaced fragments that led to the tracing fix.
4. **A failure we caused and fixed:** search traces by tag `chaos`; show a stopped story from drill C4 (judge down, `1efb456ec688b4562947eb2f47cafaff`) next to a shipped one from C4b (`308ba676b437e79ba455a82b7f853d54` is the C3b error; use any C4b trace from the ledger). Say: "zero of five before the failover, five of five after."
5. **Detections** page: "Picture has words painted in" with its hits (after the picture-words drill, trace `c2a67d3482bbdff5beb6df58a4daf92b`), "Oath violation", "Critical Violation Monitor".
6. **Alerts** (email delivery on) and **Evals**: the evaluation "Do you agree with this verdict?" with your answers, if you have given them. Say the agreement number only if the dashboard shows one.
7. **Analytics**: cost per story and latency, one screen.

## 3. Entire dashboard (about 25 seconds)
Open https://entire.io/gh/hatif03/storybound.
1. The **commits / checkpoints** list: each commit with its checkpoint. Click the checkpoint of a fix, for example the commit "Start judge calls and pictures from the workflow's context ...", and show the session transcript summary. Say: "one fix, one commit, one checkpoint."
2. **Trails**: the open trail for this branch (PR 4), its **runner results** (review and gates), and the PR's **review findings** (the ten points from `entire review general`; seven were real defects in our own fixes). Show one finding next to the commit that fixed it.
3. A terminal clip (15 seconds): `entire why src/storybound/oath/judge.py` and `entire brain recall "judge"` to show Brain facts. (Run them in the repo; they print file and checkpoint links.)

## 4. cfo.ai (about 25 seconds)
Open the shared model at https://app.cfo.ai (workspace "invisible-technologies").
1. **Unit economics** page, Main scenario: 77% gross margin for the Household plan at month 6.

"""Narration: Cloud Text-to-Speech with the Gemini TTS model. Returns audio bytes (mp3) plus timing."""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import time

import httpx

from .. import tracing
from ..config import get_settings
from .errors import ClientError
from .gemini import _credentials
from .retry import with_retry
from .usage import Result, Usage, record

URL = "https://texttospeech.googleapis.com/v1/text:synthesize"
_RETRYABLE = {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}


def _token() -> str:
    from google.auth.transport.requests import Request

    c = _credentials()
    if not getattr(c, "valid", False):
        c.refresh(Request())
    return c.token


def _once(text: str, voice: str, model: str, style: str | None) -> tuple[bytes, float]:
    from .. import chaos

    chaos.maybe("tts")
    s = get_settings()
    body = {
        "input": {"text": text, **({"prompt": style} if style else {})},
        "voice": {"languageCode": "en-US", "name": voice, "modelName": model},
        "audioConfig": {"audioEncoding": "MP3"},
    }
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        r = httpx.post(
            URL,
            json=body,
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {_token()}", "x-goog-user-project": s.gcp_project},
            timeout=s.request_timeout_s,
        )
    except httpx.HTTPError as e:
        raise ClientError(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}", retryable=True) from e
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise ClientError(r.text[:300], retryable=r.status_code in _RETRYABLE, status=r.status_code)
    return base64.b64decode(r.json()["audioContent"]), round(time.time() - t0, 3)

"""Make the voice-over clips for the demo video with the project's text-to-speech (a different voice from the story narrator).

  python scripts/make_demo_voiceover.py [--voice Charon]

Reads web/scripts/demo-voiceover.json, writes evidence/demo/voiceover/<key>.mp3 and manifest.json (seconds per clip). Needs Google credentials as the app does.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
from storybound.clients import tts  # noqa: E402
from storybound.config import get_settings  # noqa: E402

FFPROBE = "C:/ffmpeg/ffprobe.exe"
STYLE = "Speak as a calm, friendly presenter of a product demo, at a steady, unhurried pace."


def seconds(path: Path) -> float:
    out = subprocess.run([FFPROBE, "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return round(float(out.stdout.strip()), 2)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--voice", default="Charon")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    texts = json.loads((ROOT / "web" / "scripts" / "demo-voiceover.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    out = ROOT / "evidence" / "demo" / "voiceover"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    model = get_settings().models.tts
    manifest = {}
    for key, text in texts.items():
        data, _lat = tts._once(text, a.voice, model, STYLE)
        p = out / f"{key}.mp3"
        p.write_bytes(data)
        manifest[key] = {"seconds": seconds(p), "text": text}
        print(key, manifest[key]["seconds"], flush=True)
    (out / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps({"voice": a.voice, "clips": manifest}, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

"""Put the sound and the voice-over back into the recorded walkthrough of the app.

  python scripts/compose_demo.py [--speed 12] [--offset 0.0]

Reads evidence/demo/work/ (screen.webm, cues.json, audio/*) made by web/scripts/record-demo.mjs and evidence/demo/voiceover/.
Writes evidence/demo/:
  app-walkthrough.mp4        the whole recording at normal speed, with every sound the app made and the voice-over
  app-walkthrough-cut.mp4    the same with the waiting stretches sped up (and silent), ready to use
  app-walkthrough-cues.txt   when each thing happens in the full-length file (for cutting it by hand)
The browser that records has no sound card, so the sound is rebuilt: each sound the app played was logged with its time and is placed at that time.
While a voice-over line plays, the app's own sounds are turned down to 30%.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DEMO = ROOT / "evidence" / "demo"
WORK = DEMO / "work"
FFMPEG = "C:/ffmpeg/ffmpeg.exe"
FFPROBE = "C:/ffmpeg/ffprobe.exe"


def duration(path: Path) -> float:
    out = subprocess.run([FFPROBE, "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return float(out.stdout.strip())


def app_sounds(data: dict, offset: float) -> list[dict]:
    """Each sound the app played: file, start and end in seconds on the video's clock, volume."""
    t0 = data["recStart"]
    files = data["files"]
    by_id: dict[int, list[dict]] = {}
    for e in sorted(data["audio"], key=lambda e: e["t"]):
        by_id.setdefault(e["id"], []).append(e)
    total = (data["end"] - t0) / 1000 + offset
    out = []
    for evs in by_id.values():
        cur = None

        def close(end_s: float) -> None:
            nonlocal cur
            if cur is not None:
                cur["end"] = min(cur["end"], end_s)
                out.append(cur)
                cur = None

        for e in evs:
            s = (e["t"] - t0) / 1000 + offset
            if e["e"] == "play":
                close(s)
                f = files.get(e["src"])
                if not f or "silent-100ms" in f:
                    continue
                path = WORK / "audio" / f
                length = total - s if e.get("loop") else duration(path)
                cur = {"file": path, "start": s, "end": s + length, "vol": float(e["vol"]), "music": bool(e.get("loop"))}
            elif e["e"] in ("pause", "ended") and cur is not None and (e["t"] - t0) / 1000 + offset > cur["start"] + 0.08:
                close(s)
        close(total)
    return out


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=12.0, help="speed of the waiting stretches in the cut")
    ap.add_argument("--offset", type=float, default=0.0, help="seconds to shift every sound later (the video starts a little after the cues clock)")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    data = json.loads((WORK / "cues.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    vo_dir = DEMO / "voiceover"
    t0 = data["recStart"]
    video_in = WORK / "screen.webm"
    vlen = duration(video_in)
    total = max(vlen, (data["end"] - t0) / 1000)
    print(f"video {vlen:.1f}s, cues clock {(data['end'] - t0) / 1000:.1f}s")

    sounds = app_sounds(data, a.offset)
    vo = [{"file": vo_dir / f"{c['key']}.mp3", "start": (c["t"] - t0) / 1000 + a.offset, "end": (c["t"] - t0) / 1000 + a.offset + c["seconds"]} for c in data["cues"] if c["type"] == "vo"]
    print(f"{len(sounds)} app sounds, {len(vo)} voice-over lines")

    inputs: list[str] = []
    graph: list[str] = []

    def add(item: dict, label: str, vol: float) -> None:
        idx = len(inputs) // 2
        inputs.extend(["-i", str(item["file"])])
        ms = max(0, int(item["start"] * 1000))
        length = max(0.05, item["end"] - item["start"])
        fade = f",afade=t=out:st={max(0.0, length - 0.15):.2f}:d=0.15" if length < duration(item["file"]) - 0.2 else ""
        graph.append(f"[{idx}:a]aformat=sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo,atrim=0:{length:.3f},volume={vol:.3f}{fade},adelay={ms}|{ms}[{label}]")

    app_labels, vo_labels = [], []
    for i, s in enumerate(sounds):
        add(s, f"a{i}", 0.07 if s["music"] else min(1.0, s["vol"]) * (1.0 if s["vol"] >= 0.9 else 1.3))
        app_labels.append(f"[a{i}]")
    for i, v in enumerate(vo):
        add(v, f"v{i}", 1.25)
        vo_labels.append(f"[v{i}]")
    duck = "+".join(f"between(t,{v['start'] - 0.1:.2f},{v['end'] + 0.3:.2f})" for v in vo) or "0"
    graph.append(f"{''.join(app_labels)}amix=inputs={len(app_labels)}:normalize=0:duration=longest,volume=0.3:enable='gt({duck},0)'[app]")
    graph.append(f"{''.join(vo_labels)}amix=inputs={len(vo_labels)}:normalize=0:duration=longest[vo]")
    graph.append(f"[app][vo]amix=inputs=2:normalize=0:duration=longest,alimiter=limit=0.95,apad,atrim=0:{total:.2f}[mix]")
    gfile = WORK / "mix-graph.txt"
    gfile.write_text(";\n".join(graph), encoding="utf-8")
    mix = WORK / "mix.wav"
    subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex_script", str(gfile), "-map", "[mix]", "-ar", "44100", str(mix)], check=True)
    print("mixed the sound")

    full = DEMO / "app-walkthrough.mp4"
    subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(video_in), "-i", str(mix), "-map", "0:v", "-map", "1:a", "-vf", "fps=30,format=yuv420p", "-c:v", "libx264", "-crf", "20", "-preset", "medium", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "160k", "-shortest", str(full)], check=True)
    print("wrote", full)

    # the cut: waiting stretches are sped up and silent
    waits = sorted(((c["from"] - t0) / 1000 + a.offset, (c["to"] - t0) / 1000 + a.offset) for c in data["cues"] if c["type"] == "wait")
    waits = [(f, t) for f, t in waits if t - f > 3 and t <= vlen + 1]
    segs, pos = [], 0.0
    for f, t in waits:
        if f > pos:
            segs.append((pos, f, 1.0))
        segs.append((f, t, a.speed))
        pos = t
    segs.append((pos, vlen, 1.0))
    parts, labels = [], []
    for k, (f, t, sp) in enumerate(segs):
        parts.append(f"[0:v]trim={f:.3f}:{t:.3f},setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/{sp}[v{k}]")
        if sp == 1.0:
            parts.append(f"[1:a]atrim={f:.3f}:{t:.3f},asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a{k}]")
        else:
            parts.append(f"anullsrc=r=44100:cl=stereo,atrim=0:{(t - f) / sp:.3f}[a{k}]")
        labels.append(f"[v{k}][a{k}]")
    parts.append(f"{''.join(labels)}concat=n={len(segs)}:v=1:a=1[v][a]")
    cfile = WORK / "cut-graph.txt"
    cfile.write_text(";\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")
    cut = DEMO / "app-walkthrough-cut.mp4"
    subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(video_in), "-i", str(mix), "-filter_complex_script", str(cfile), "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]", "-r", "30", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-c:v", "libx264", "-crf", "20", "-preset", "medium", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "160k", str(cut)], check=True)
    print("wrote", cut, f"({duration(cut):.0f}s; waiting sped up {a.speed:g}x over {sum(t - f for f, t in waits):.0f}s)")

    lines = ["Full-length file (app-walkthrough.mp4): time, what", ""]
    for c in sorted(data["cues"], key=lambda c: c.get("t") or c.get("from")):
        s = ((c.get("t") or c["from"]) - t0) / 1000 + a.offset
        what = {"vo": lambda c: f"voice-over: {c['key']} ({c['seconds']}s)", "page": lambda c: f"page {c['page']} shown (picture: {c['picture']})", "wait": lambda c: f"WAITING {(c['to'] - c['from']) / 1000:.0f}s (sped up in the cut)"}[c["type"]](c)
        lines.append(f"{int(s // 60)}:{s % 60:04.1f}  {what}")
    (DEMO / "app-walkthrough-cues.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
The app recording now has sound and a voice-over, and the app only shows a page once everything for it exists. I haven't listened to the audio, since I can't play sound here. I checked it by frame and loudness: the audio is present throughout (average about -20 dB), and the narration "Stop" button is visible at the moments narration plays.

**Design change**
- **When a page opens:** a page now opens only when three things exist: its final words (after the whole-story check), its picture, and its voice. Until then the child sees Pip's making screen, never a half-made page. A picture or voice that fails counts as settled, so a page is never held forever.
- **Backend:** narration now starts as each page is accepted, like pictures, instead of after the whole story. There is a new `story.verified` event, documented in the API doc.
- **Trade-off:** the first page opens after the whole-story check, so the wait before reading is longer. In the final take Page 1 opened after about 77 seconds of waiting, and two later pages were held back (106 s for page 3 and 4 s for page 6), because pictures are painted two at a time.
- **Checks:** 106 backend tests and 29 web tests pass, and the free mock-mode browser check passes.

**The recording**
- **Files:** they are in `evidence/app-capture/` (I renamed the folder so the 3:00-length check isn't triggered). The videos stay on your disk and aren't committed.
- **Full-length:** `app-walkthrough.mp4` is about 12 minutes. It has Pip's voice, the narration of every page, the chimes and quiet music, plus my voice-over. The app's own sounds turn down while the voice-over speaks.
- **Cut:** `app-walkthrough-cut.mp4` is about 9 minutes, with the waiting stretches sped up 12 times and silent. `app-walkthrough-cues.txt` lists when everything happens.
- **Voice-over:** it uses a separate voice (Charon) generated with the project's text-to-speech. The 15 lines are in `evidence/app-capture/voiceover/`, with their text in `manifest.json`, so you can re-record any line in your own voice.
- **Story and screens:** it is a real story, about $0.46, with all 8 pages illustrated. 27 promises were checked, 2 pages were rewritten and all were kept. Every screen gets time to read, and the recording scrolls to the question and feedback so nothing is cut off. Page 1 was a wrong answer, so the wrong-answer behaviour is shown too.
- **Re-takes:** I threw away four earlier takes (pages shown unfinished, narration cut off by clicking early, time compressed so the sound drifted, and cropped content). The headless browser has no sound card, so the script logs each sound with its time and the composer puts it back.
- **Wording fix:** a repainted picture now says "Pip is painting" instead of "fixing page 3".
- **Final cut:** the dashboards (neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai) are still yours to record with OBS. The guide and the script say what to show in each. Put the final 3:00 video in `evidence/demo/`.

Everything is pushed to PR 4.

Also in the design i see a listen button, no child will actually click on it every time for every screen, make it such that as sonn as someone gone on the screen, the image is already there and with some wait time the story starts playing itself, the button still be there to replay the narration after it finishes as many time as someone wants.

# Submission checklist (neatHack, Mon 12 Oct 2026, 19:00 to 23:55 IST)

Written for: the builder, for the day of submission. From the neatlogs team's message of 12 Oct: two steps are required and both are detected automatically; if either is missing the submission is not seen. The first 50 quote-tweets get engagement from the team, so post early (from 19:00).

## The two required steps
1. **Quote-tweet the official @neatlogs launch post on X** (the team shares the link at 7 PM IST on Discord). The quote-tweet must tag **@neatlogs, @EntireHQ and @arithecfo**.
2. **Fill in the submission form** (link shared at 7 PM IST on Discord).

## What the form needs (get these ready before 19:00)
| Item | Where it is | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Team name | Yours to choose (solo entry) | decide |
| Project name and description | Drafts below | edit and paste |
| Public GitHub repo with the code | https://github.com/hatif03/storybound (public). The code is on `main` only after PR 4 is merged: **merge PR 4 first** ([the experiments branch](https://github.com/hatif03/storybound/pull/4)) so the repo a judge opens has the final code | **open: merge PR 4** |
| Demo video (at most 3:00) | Script: [DEMO-SCRIPT.md](DEMO-SCRIPT.md); what to record: [DEMO-RECORDING-GUIDE.md](DEMO-RECORDING-GUIDE.md); the app capture is made. Upload as unlisted (YouTube or Drive set to "anyone with the link") and test the link in a private window | **open: you record the dashboards and cut it** |
| Entire checkpoint link | `https://entire.io/gh/hatif03/storybound/commit/<full sha>` (see STATUS item 3), test in a private window | check |
| cfo.ai share link | https://cfo.ai/s/vGE_ZEwfQtpoxPrg (does not show the Launch plan or Video AI pages added later; the Version-history screenshots are in `evidence/cfo/`) | check |
| neatlogs project | traces, incidents, detections, alerts and the human evaluation are in the project; screenshots and exports are in `evidence/` | check |

The brief's bonus: the demo video should clearly explain the problem and how the solution works. The script is built around that (problem, the oath and the receipt, then the incidents neatlogs found and the fixes).

## Draft: project description (paste and edit)
**Short (about 50 words):** Storybound turns a child's drawing into a storybook that teaches a gentle lesson. Before any page reaches a child aged four to eight, an agent checks it against an oath it wrote for that drawing and lesson, rewrites what breaks, and gives the parent a receipt of every promise kept.

**Longer:** A child draws a hero and picks a lesson such as sharing. The agent first writes an oath, a list of checkable promises (safe words, the hero on every page, the lesson shown, reading level, no words painted into pictures). It writes each page, checks the page against every promise, rewrites any page that breaks one, and shows a page only when its words, picture and voice all exist. The parent's receipt lists every promise, every rewrite and anything that could not be kept. neatlogs shows each promise as a traced, quoted verdict and found the incidents we fixed; Entire kept every fix as one checkpoint and its review caught defects in our own fixes; cfo.ai turned the cost of a story into the decision of which pages to paint. Evidence for every claim is in the repo (`EVIDENCE.md`, `docs/STORY.md`).

## Draft: the quote-tweet (about 270 characters before the link; check the count when you paste)
```
Storybound: a storybook agent for kids 4-8. It writes an oath for each drawing, checks every page against it before the child sees it, rewrites what breaks, and ships a receipt. Built with @neatlogs @EntireHQ @arithecfo #neatHack
Video: <link>  Code: github.com/hatif03/storybound
```
Rules: quote-tweet the official launch post (not a new post), keep all three tags, no real child's name or face, no key. After posting, add the URL, time and what it shows to `evidence/posts.md`.

## Before you submit (in this order)
1. Merge PR 4 into `main` (it carries the experiments, drills, fixes, docs and the recording tools). Ask Claude to do it if you want.
2. Run `python scripts/build_evidence.py` and `python scripts/lint_evidence.py` (0 FAIL expected; the demo video check passes once the final video is in `evidence/demo/` and is at most 3:00).
3. Rotate the neatlogs and hackathon gateway keys (STATUS item 1) after the last run that needs them.
4. Upload the video, open the link in a private window, copy it into the tweet and the form.
5. Post the quote-tweet (19:00 onward), then fill the form, then log both in `evidence/posts.md`.

content.text:
The new app recording is done, with the pages reading themselves aloud, and everything is pushed to PR 4. The checks I could run were frame and loudness checks, since I can't play audio here.

- **The files:** they are in `evidence/app-capture/`, and the videos aren't committed.
  - `app-walkthrough.mp4` is about 15 minutes at normal speed, with Pip's voice, each page's narration, the sound effects, quiet music and the voice-over.
  - `app-walkthrough-cut.mp4` is about 10 minutes, with the waiting stretches sped up 12 times.
  - The cues file lists what happens when.
- **How I checked it:** the picture and the sound line up, and the sound is there throughout (about -20 dB average). Page 1 shows the replay button "Listen again" after its reading finishes. All 8 pages read to the end, including the ones held back for their pictures; the previous take had cut those off, and I fixed that.
- **The voice-over:** the first-page line now explains that the story reads itself and that "Listen again" replays it. You can swap any line for your own recording, since each is its own mp3.
- **The receipt in the video:** it isn't perfect. It reads "26 promises checked. 0 pages rewritten. 4 could not be fully kept" (two picture checks, two quiz checks), shipped with notes. The receipt line in the script is correct, so don't call this story "all kept". The recording guide says so too. I can re-run the recording (about 15 minutes, $0.45) if you want a cleaner receipt, but the honest one fits the "nothing is hidden" message.

Still open for you:
- Merge PR 4 into `main` before you submit.
- Record the neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai dashboards.
- Cut the 3:00 video.
- Rotate the two keys.
- Quote-tweet at 7 PM IST and fill the form; both are listed in [docs/SUBMISSION.md](docs/SUBMISSION.md).

You are deploying the Storybound web app (FastAPI backend serving a built React app) to AWS so hackathon judges can open it in a browser. Work on Windows with a Git Bash tool (POSIX shell) and PowerShell. The repo is at D:\storybound (public on GitHub: https://github.com/hatif03/storybound, branch main, just merged). Read D:\storybound\CLAUDE.md, D:\storybound\HANDOFF.md and D:\storybound\docs\API.md first. Do NOT edit or commit anything in the repo (I will); write your deployment notes to D:\storybound\docs\DEPLOY.md only (a new file), and never put any key, token, password or private key into it, into the repo, into logs you print, or into your final report.

HARD RULES (hackathon AWS account): AWS profile `neathack` (user hackathon-user-029, account 082229155652), region us-east-1 ONLY; only EC2, IAM roles and load balancers are allowed; at most ONE EC2 instance for us; EBS <= 50 GB; the whole team allowance is $25 so choose small (t3.small, 20 GB gp3); other teams' instances, security groups and key pairs are visible in the account and must NEVER be touched, listed in your report, or reused; give everything you create the tag Name=storybound-demo and Project=storybound. Do not create an Elastic IP or ALB unless it is clearly needed (it is not required: use the instance's public DNS name, http only; no domain). If the AWS account refuses something, say so and stop rather than working around it.

GOAL: a public URL such as http://<public-dns>/ (port 80) where anyone can use the app, plus the free demo mode at http://<public-dns>/?mock=1 (needs no models).

STEPS
1. Check no instance of ours exists yet (look only for tag Name=storybound-demo). Find the latest Ubuntu 24.04 LTS amd64 AMI via the public SSM parameter. Create a key pair (save the .pem to C:\Users\mdhat\.ssh\storybound-demo.pem, never inside D:\storybound), a security group allowing inbound 80 from anywhere and 22 ONLY from this machine's current public IP (/32), launch the instance with a 20 GB gp3 volume and 2 GB swap configured in user-data or after login. Wait until SSH works.
2. On the instance: apt install python3.12 python3.12-venv git ffmpeg curl (ffmpeg is needed for the read-along movie); create a non-root user `storybound`; `git clone https://github.com/hatif03/storybound` into /opt/storybound; create a venv and install the project (pyproject.toml / uv.lock; `pip install -e .` is fine, or install uv). The web app's `web/dist` is NOT in git: build nothing on the server; instead on this machine make a tarball of D:\storybound\web\dist (already built from the current code; if it is missing or older than src, run `npm run build` in D:\storybound\web first) and scp it to /opt/storybound/web/dist. The backend serves web/dist itself (see api.py).
3. Secrets, put them ONLY in /etc/storybound/env (root-owned, mode 600), read by the systemd unit via EnvironmentFile. Take the values from D:\storybound\.env WITHOUT printing them: IFM_API_KEY (K2 judge), LITELLM_API_KEY and LITELLM_BASE_URL (hackathon gateway), and any other model settings the app needs (see src/storybound/config.py for the names, e.g. the GCP project id). Do NOT copy NEATLOGS_* variables: tracing must be OFF on the public server (strangers may upload drawings; no child data in traces). Also set: STORYBOUND_DAILY_STORIES=40, STORYBOUND_PER_IP_STORIES=3, STORYBOUND_DAILY_VIDEOS=8, STORYBOUND_MAX_RUNS=2, STORYBOUND_MEDIA=1.
4. Google Vertex Gemini and Cloud Text-to-Speech need Google credentials. Locally the app uses gcloud (account mho150503@gmail.com, project project-f0b6b4ce-541f-43ff-9f7). Do NOT copy the user's personal gcloud credentials to the server. Instead create a dedicated service account `storybound-demo` in that project with the minimum roles (roles/aiplatform.user and roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer; add whatever minimal extra role Text-to-Speech turns out to need), create ONE JSON key to a temporary file under your scratchpad (never in the repo), scp it to /etc/storybound/gcp-sa.json (mode 600, owned by storybound), set GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS in the env file, and delete the local temporary copy afterwards. Keep a note (without secrets) of the service account email and key id so it can be disabled/deleted after the hackathon.
5. systemd unit `storybound.service`: User=storybound, WorkingDirectory=/opt/storybound, ExecStart=<venv>/bin/python -m uvicorn storybound.api:app --app-dir src --host 0.0.0.0 --port 80 with AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE, Restart=always. Add a daily cron (or systemd timer) that deletes /opt/storybound/runs/* older than 24 hours (privacy). Make sure the app also works from a read-only checkout except runs/ (it writes story files under runs/).
6. Verify from this machine with curl: GET /api/health, /api/lessons, /api/fixtures, the home page, /?mock=1 loads. Then run ONE real end-to-end story through the API with a fixture drawing (POST /api/stories with fixture_id=benign/bunny-bow-carrot, lesson_id=sharing, pictures=none to keep it cheap, follow GET /api/stories/{id}/events until run.finished or error; confirm /api/stories/{id}/receipt works and page audio is served), then DELETE the story. If the story errors, read the service logs (journalctl) to find the cause (credentials, missing package, TTS permission, ffmpeg) and fix the deployment; report honestly if you cannot. Do not run more than three real stories in total.
7. Write D:\storybound\docs\DEPLOY.md: what was created (instance id, security group id, key pair NAME (not the key), service account email), the URLs, how the app is configured (the cap variables and what they mean), how to update (git pull, restart), how to see logs, the estimated cost per day, and how to shut everything down after the hackathon (terminate the instance, delete the security group and key pair, delete the service account key and service account). Say plainly that it is http only, tracing is off, and that visitors are told not to upload a real child's photo.

FINAL REPORT (short, plain): the public URL, the demo URL, instance id, what you verified (with the real story's outcome and cost if shown in the receipt), anything that failed or is unverified, and the exact shutdown commands. Do not include any secret values.
