# Why a parent would want Storybound, and who it helps

Written for: parents, teachers, librarians and anyone who is not an engineer. No jargon; every number points to a file in this repository.

## The problem in one minute
Computers can now write a bedtime story about your child's own drawing in seconds. That is wonderful and a little frightening. A story model is a fast, fluent writer that has no idea what is right for a five-year-old, and nobody is watching it. In our own experiment, the same story writer, left alone, slipped at least one broken promise into **27 of 28** stories: a lesson that never appeared, a question where the right answer was always the first one, sentences too hard for the age, and sometimes an unkind line. Reading every story first is exactly what a busy parent cannot do, and if a child is on a tablet the parent is not there to check.

So today a parent has two choices: do not use these tools, or trust them blindly. Storybound is a third choice: **use them, and check them**.

## What Storybound does, in four steps
1. **A child draws a hero** (or a grown-up photographs a drawing) and picks a lesson: sharing, honesty, kindness or patience.
2. **A helper writes down its promises first.** Before there is any story, the agent writes a short oath for this drawing and this lesson: it will keep to age-appropriate words, show the hero on every page, actually teach the lesson, avoid scary or unkind things, and not paint stray words into pictures. A grown-up can add a promise of their own ("nobody in the story is left out").
3. **It checks every page before the child sees it.** A page that breaks a promise is rewritten, and only then shown. Each page comes with a picture and a warm voice reading it aloud, then a gentle choice ("What should Sam do with the blocks?") where a wrong answer is never a scolding. After the story there is a short quiz and a picture game, and the app can make a read-along movie of the story.
4. **The grown-up gets a receipt.** A plain page behind a grown-up gate says how many promises were checked, which pages had to be rewritten, and anything that could not be fully kept. Nothing is hidden. The result: **0 of 28** stories shipped with a broken promise when every page was checked, against 27 of 28 without.

Think of it as the nutrition label for a bedtime story.

## Why a family would try it
- **It makes a story out of what the child made.** Their own drawing becomes the hero. That is a reason to pick up a pencil, not only a screen.
- **You do not have to read it first.** The checking happens before the child sees a page, and the receipt tells you afterwards what it did.
- **It reads to the child.** A page opens, the picture is already there, and after a short pause the story reads itself aloud. A child who cannot read yet, or who is learning English, can listen on their own and replay any page.
- **It is gentle by design.** No accounts, no ads, no purchases. No timers, streaks, scores or "come back tomorrow". After two stories Pip suggests resting the eyes. Everything that throws work away needs a hold, not a tap. A parent can make the app forget a story, which deletes it.
- **It gives parents something to talk about.** Each story ends with a question for a grown-up to ask ("What do you like to share with your friends?").

## Community impact: why it matters beyond one family
- **A pattern other children's tools can copy.** The idea that matters is not a story app. It is that anything an AI makes for children should come with promises written down in advance, checked before delivery, and a receipt a parent can read. This repository is open so anyone building for children can reuse it.
- **Trust that can be checked.** Every claim here is backed by a recorded run in `evidence/`. We also say what did not work (a cheaper writer failed three stories in ten; a mistake of our own made the check screen look like a refusal) and how we fixed it.
- **Cheap enough to give away.** A story costs about two cents of text and roughly twelve cents with pictures and a voice (measured with neatlogs; modelled with cfo.ai). That puts it within reach of schools, libraries and community groups, not only paying households. Video clips, which would cost far more, are left out on purpose ([BUSINESS.md](BUSINESS.md)).
- **Reading aloud for children who are read to less.** Parents who work long hours, are learning the language, or find reading hard can still give a child a story that reads aloud, in a calm voice, with a lesson that matches what the family cares about. We do not claim it replaces a parent; a gentle conversation card nudges the grown-up to join in.
- **Privacy by default.** The drawing is not kept after the story, nothing is sold, and no real child's data is used in our traces, tests or posts.

## What it is not (honesty matters for children's tools)
- It is a prototype built in three days, tested with fixture drawings and one family tester, not a product tested with many children. Ten to thirty stories per experiment is a small sample.
- The checker is another AI model, not a person; the human review of its verdicts is only just under way ([TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md)).
- Stories are in English; a Hindi or Spanish caption on a drawing is ignored, never repeated, but we have not built translation.
- A story can still be imperfect; that is why the receipt exists. In our own demo recording the receipt reads "26 promises checked, 4 could not be fully kept", and it says so.

## See it
- The three-minute video, the full tour with the grown-up side, and the live app: see the top of the [README](../README.md).
- The numbers behind this page: [STORY.md](STORY.md), [HR-014](../evidence/hardening/HR-014.md), [HR-015](../evidence/hardening/HR-015.md), [BUSINESS.md](BUSINESS.md).

"""Put the sound and the voice-over back into a recorded walkthrough of the app.

  python scripts/compose_demo.py [--dir evidence/app-capture] [--name app-walkthrough] [--speed 12]

Reads <dir>/work/ (frames.json + frames/, cues.json, audio/*, optional movie.mp4) made by web/scripts/record-demo.mjs or record-features.mjs, and
<dir>/voiceover/. Writes into <dir>/:
  <name>.mp4         the whole recording at normal speed, with every sound the app made and the voice-over
  <name>-cut.mp4     the same with the waiting stretches sped up (and silent)
  <name>-cues.txt    when each thing happens in the full-length file
  apponly.wav        the app's own sounds without the voice-over (work/apponly.wav), used when a short clip of the real narration is wanted
A cue of type "movie" is replaced, in both files, by the real movie file (full frame, with its own sound), because the headless browser cannot capture the
sound of a playing video. The browser that records has no sound card: each sound the app played was logged with its time and is placed at that time.
While a voice-over line plays, the app's own sounds are turned down to 30%.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FFMPEG = "C:/ffmpeg/ffmpeg.exe"
FFPROBE = "C:/ffmpeg/ffprobe.exe"
W, H = 1440, 810


def duration(path: Path) -> float:
    out = subprocess.run([FFPROBE, "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return float(out.stdout.strip())


def app_sounds(data: dict, work: Path, t0: int, total: float) -> list[dict]:
    """Each sound the app played: file, start and end in seconds on the video's clock, volume."""
    files = data["files"]
    by_id: dict[int, list[dict]] = {}
    for e in sorted(data["audio"], key=lambda e: e["t"]):
        by_id.setdefault(e["id"], []).append(e)
    out = []
    for evs in by_id.values():
        cur = None

        def close(end_s: float) -> None:
            nonlocal cur
            if cur is not None:
                cur["end"] = min(cur["end"], end_s)
                out.append(cur)
                cur = None

        for e in evs:
            s = (e["t"] - t0) / 1000
            if e["e"] == "play":
                close(s)
                f = files.get(e["src"])
                if not f or "silent-100ms" in f:
                    continue
                path = work / "audio" / f
                length = total - s if e.get("loop") else duration(path)
                cur = {"file": path, "start": s, "end": s + length, "vol": float(e["vol"]), "music": bool(e.get("loop"))}
            elif e["e"] in ("pause", "ended") and cur is not None and s > cur["start"] + 0.08:
                close(s)
        close(total)
    return out


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dir", default="evidence/app-capture")
    ap.add_argument("--name", default="app-walkthrough")
    ap.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=12.0, help="speed of the waiting stretches in the cut")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    base = ROOT / a.dir
    work = base / "work"
    data = json.loads((work / "cues.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    frames = json.loads((work / "frames.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))  # [epoch ms, file]: each frame is shown from its time until the next frame's
    t0 = frames[0][0]
    end_ms = max(data["end"], frames[-1][0] + 1000)
    video_in = work / "screen.mp4"
    if not video_in.exists():
        rows = []
        for i, (t, name) in enumerate(frames):
            nxt = frames[i + 1][0] if i + 1 < len(frames) else end_ms
            rows.append(f"file 'frames/{name}'")
            rows.append(f"duration {max(0.001, (nxt - t) / 1000):.3f}")
        rows.append(f"file 'frames/{frames[-1][1]}'")  # the concat demuxer ignores the duration of the last entry unless it is repeated
        (work / "frames.txt").write_text(chr(10).join(rows), encoding="utf-8")
        subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", str(work / "frames.txt"), "-vf", f"fps=30,scale={W}:{H},format=yuv420p", "-c:v", "libx264", "-crf", "20", "-preset", "veryfast", str(video_in)], check=True)
    vlen = duration(video_in)
    total = max(vlen, (end_ms - t0) / 1000)
    print(f"video {vlen:.1f}s, cues clock {(end_ms - t0) / 1000:.1f}s")

    vo_dir = base / "voiceover"
    sounds = app_sounds(data, work, t0, total)
    vo = [{"file": vo_dir / f"{c['key']}.mp3", "start": (c["t"] - t0) / 1000, "end": (c["t"] - t0) / 1000 + c["seconds"]} for c in data["cues"] if c["type"] == "vo"]
    print(f"{len(sounds)} app sounds, {len(vo)} voice-over lines")

    inputs: list[str] = []
    graph: list[str] = []

    def add(item: dict, label: str, vol: float) -> None:
        idx = len(inputs) // 2
        inputs.extend(["-i", str(item["file"])])
        ms = max(0, int(item["start"] * 1000))
        length = max(0.05, item["end"] - item["start"])
        fade = f",afade=t=out:st={max(0.0, length - 0.15):.2f}:d=0.15" if length < duration(item["file"]) - 0.2 else ""
        graph.append(f"[{idx}:a]aformat=sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo,atrim=0:{length:.3f},volume={vol:.3f}{fade},adelay={ms}|{ms}[{label}]")

    app_labels, vo_labels = [], []
    for i, s in enumerate(sounds):
        add(s, f"a{i}", 0.07 if s["music"] else min(1.0, s["vol"]) * (1.0 if s["vol"] >= 0.9 else 1.3))
        app_labels.append(f"[a{i}]")
    for i, v in enumerate(vo):
        add(v, f"v{i}", 1.25)
        vo_labels.append(f"[v{i}]")
    duck = "+".join(f"between(t,{v['start'] - 0.1:.2f},{v['end'] + 0.3:.2f})" for v in vo) or "0"
    graph.append(f"{''.join(app_labels)}amix=inputs={len(app_labels)}:normalize=0:duration=longest,volume=2.0,apad,atrim=0:{total:.2f},asplit=2[appraw][appduck]")
    graph.append(f"[appduck]volume=0.3:enable='gt({duck},0)'[app]")
    graph.append(f"{''.join(vo_labels)}amix=inputs={len(vo_labels)}:normalize=0:duration=longest[vo]")
    graph.append(f"[app][vo]amix=inputs=2:normalize=0:duration=longest,volume=2.0,alimiter=limit=0.95,apad,atrim=0:{total:.2f}[mix]")
    (work / "mix-graph.txt").write_text(";\n".join(graph), encoding="utf-8")
    mix, apponly = work / "mix.wav", work / "apponly.wav"
    subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex_script", str(work / "mix-graph.txt"), "-map", "[mix]", "-ar", "44100", str(mix), "-map", "[appraw]", "-ar", "44100", str(apponly)], check=True)
    print("mixed the sound")

    movie_file = work / "movie.mp4"

    def cue_span(c: dict) -> tuple[float, float]:
        return (c["from"] - t0) / 1000, (c["to"] - t0) / 1000

    movies = sorted(cue_span(c) for c in data["cues"] if c["type"] == "movie" and movie_file.exists())
    waits = sorted(cue_span(c) for c in data["cues"] if c["type"] == "wait")
    waits = [(f, t) for f, t in waits if t - f > 3 and t <= vlen + 1]

    def segments(fast: bool) -> list[tuple[str, float, float, float]]:
        marks = [(f, t, "movie", 1.0) for f, t in movies] + ([(f, t, "screen", a.speed) for f, t in waits] if fast else [])
        marks.sort()
        segs, pos = [], 0.0
        for f, t, kind, sp in marks:
            f = max(f, pos)
            if f > pos:
                segs.append(("screen", pos, f, 1.0))
            if t > f:
                segs.append((kind, f, t, sp))
            pos = max(pos, t)
        segs.append(("screen", pos, vlen, 1.0))
        return [s for s in segs if s[2] - s[1] > 0.05]

    def render(out: Path, segs: list[tuple[str, float, float, float]]) -> None:
        parts, labels = [], []
        for k, (kind, f, t, sp) in enumerate(segs):
            if kind == "movie":
                d = t - f
                parts.append(f"[2:v]trim=0:{d:.3f},setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad={W}:{H}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,fps=30[v{k}]")
                parts.append(f"[2:a]aformat=sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo,atrim=0:{d:.3f},asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a{k}]")
            else:
                parts.append(f"[0:v]trim={f:.3f}:{t:.3f},setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/{sp}[v{k}]")
                if sp == 1.0:
                    parts.append(f"[1:a]atrim={f:.3f}:{t:.3f},asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a{k}]")
                else:
                    parts.append(f"anullsrc=r=44100:cl=stereo,atrim=0:{(t - f) / sp:.3f}[a{k}]")
            labels.append(f"[v{k}][a{k}]")
        parts.append(f"{''.join(labels)}concat=n={len(segs)}:v=1:a=1[v][a]")
        gf = work / f"{out.stem}-graph.txt"
        gf.write_text(";\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")
        ins = ["-i", str(video_in), "-i", str(mix)] + (["-i", str(movie_file)] if movie_file.exists() else [])
        subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", *ins, "-filter_complex_script", str(gf), "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]", "-r", "30", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-c:v", "libx264", "-crf", "20", "-preset", "medium", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "160k", str(out)], check=True)

    full, cut = base / f"{a.name}.mp4", base / f"{a.name}-cut.mp4"
    render(full, segments(False))
    print("wrote", full, f"({duration(full):.0f}s)")
    render(cut, segments(True))
    print("wrote", cut, f"({duration(cut):.0f}s; waiting sped up {a.speed:g}x over {sum(t - f for f, t in waits):.0f}s)")

    lines = [f"Full-length file ({a.name}.mp4): time, what", ""]
    for c in sorted(data["cues"], key=lambda c: c.get("t") or c.get("from")):
        s = ((c.get("t") or c["from"]) - t0) / 1000
        what = {
            "vo": lambda c: f"voice-over: {c['key']} ({c['seconds']}s)",
            "page": lambda c: f"page {c['page']} shown (picture: {c['picture']})",
            "wait": lambda c: f"WAITING {(c['to'] - c['from']) / 1000:.0f}s {c.get('label', '')} (sped up in the cut)",
            "movie": lambda c: f"the real movie plays ({(c['to'] - c['from']) / 1000:.0f}s)",
        }[c["type"]](c)
        lines.append(f"{int(s // 60)}:{s % 60:04.1f}  {what}")
    (base / f"{a.name}-cues.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        rows.append(f"file 'frames/{frames[-1][1]}'")  # the concat demuxer ignores the duration of the last entry unless it is repeated
        (work / "frames.txt").write_text(chr(10).join(rows), encoding="utf-8")
        subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", str(work / "frames.txt"), "-vf", f"fps=30,scale={W}:{H},format=yuv420p", "-c:v", "libx264", "-crf", "20", "-preset", "veryfast", str(video_in)], check=True)
    vlen = duration(video_in)
    total = max(vlen, (end_ms - t0) / 1000)
    print(f"video {vlen:.1f}s, cues clock {(end_ms - t0) / 1000:.1f}s")

    vo_dir = base / "voiceover"
    sounds = app_sounds(data, work, t0, total)
    vo = [{"file": vo_dir / f"{c['key']}.mp3", "start": (c["t"] - t0) / 1000, "end": (c["t"] - t0) / 1000 + c["seconds"]} for c in data["cues"] if c["type"] == "vo"]
    print(f"{len(sounds)} app sounds, {len(vo)} voice-over lines")

    inputs: list[str] = []
    graph: list[str] = []

    def add(item: dict, label: str, vol: float) -> None:
        idx = len(inputs) // 2
        inputs.extend(["-i", str(item["file"])])
        ms = max(0, int(item["start"] * 1000))
        length = max(0.05, item["end"] - item["start"])
        fade = f",afade=t=out:st={max(0.0, length - 0.15):.2f}:d=0.15" if length < duration(item["file"]) - 0.2 else ""
        graph.append(f"[{idx}:a]aformat=sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo,atrim=0:{length:.3f},volume={vol:.3f}{fade},adelay={ms}|{ms}[{label}]")

    app_labels, vo_labels = [], []
    for i, s in enumerate(sounds):
        add(s, f"a{i}", 0.07 if s["music"] else min(1.0, s["vol"]) * (1.0 if s["vol"] >= 0.9 else 1.3))
        app_labels.append(f"[a{i}]")
    for i, v in enumerate(vo):
        add(v, f"v{i}", 1.25)
        vo_labels.append(f"[v{i}]")
    duck = "+".join(f"between(t,{v['start'] - 0.1:.2f},{v['end'] + 0.3:.2f})" for v in vo) or "0"
    graph.append(f"{''.join(app_labels)}amix=inputs={len(app_labels)}:normalize=0:duration=longest,volume=2.0,apad,atrim=0:{total:.2f},asplit=2[appraw][appduck]")
    graph.append(f"[appduck]volume=0.3:enable='gt({duck},0)'[app]")
    graph.append(f"{''.join(vo_labels)}amix=inputs={len(vo_labels)}:normalize=0:duration=longest[vo]")
    graph.append(f"[app][vo]amix=inputs=2:normalize=0:duration=longest,volume=2.0,alimiter=limit=0.95,apad,atrim=0:{total:.2f}[mix]")
    (work / "mix-graph.txt").write_text(";\n".join(graph), encoding="utf-8")
    mix, apponly = work / "mix.wav", work / "apponly.wav"
    subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex_script", str(work / "mix-graph.txt"), "-map", "[mix]", "-ar", "44100", str(mix), "-map", "[appraw]", "-ar", "44100", str(apponly)], check=True)
    print("mixed the sound")

    movie_file = work / "movie.mp4"

    def cue_span(c: dict) -> tuple[float, float]:
        return (c["from"] - t0) / 1000, (c["to"] - t0) / 1000

    movies = sorted(cue_span(c) for c in data["cues"] if c["type"] == "movie" and movie_file.exists())
    waits = sorted(cue_span(c) for c in data["cues"] if c["type"] == "wait")
    waits = [(f, t) for f, t in waits if t - f > 3 and t <= vlen + 1]

    def segments(fast: bool) -> list[tuple[str, float, float, float]]:
        marks = [(f, t, "movie", 1.0) for f, t in movies] + ([(f, t, "screen", a.speed) for f, t in waits] if fast else [])
        marks.sort()
        segs, pos = [], 0.0
        for f, t, kind, sp in marks:
            f = max(f, pos)
            if f > pos:
                segs.append(("screen", pos, f, 1.0))
            if t > f:
                segs.append((kind, f, t, sp))
            pos = max(pos, t)
        segs.append(("screen", pos, vlen, 1.0))
        return [s for s in segs if s[2] - s[1] > 0.05]

    def render(out: Path, segs: list[tuple[str, float, float, float]]) -> None:
        parts, labels = [], []
        for k, (kind, f, t, sp) in enumerate(segs):
            if kind == "movie":
                d = t - f
                parts.append(f"[2:v]trim=0:{d:.3f},setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad={W}:{H}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,fps=30[v{k}]")
                parts.append(f"[2:a]aformat=sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo,atrim=0:{d:.3f},asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a{k}]")
            else:
                parts.append(f"[0:v]trim={f:.3f}:{t:.3f},setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/{sp}[v{k}]")
                if sp == 1.0:
                    parts.append(f"[1:a]atrim={f:.3f}:{t:.3f},asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a{k}]")
                else:
                    parts.append(f"anullsrc=r=44100:cl=stereo,atrim=0:{(t - f) / sp:.3f}[a{k}]")
            labels.append(f"[v{k}][a{k}]")
        parts.append(f"{''.join(labels)}concat=n={len(segs)}:v=1:a=1[v][a]")
        gf = work / f"{out.stem}-graph.txt"
        gf.write_text(";\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")
        ins = ["-i", str(video_in), "-i", str(mix)] + (["-i", str(movie_file)] if movie_file.exists() else [])
        subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", *ins, "-filter_complex_script", str(gf), "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]", "-r", "30", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-c:v", "libx264", "-crf", "20", "-preset", "medium", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "160k", str(out)], check=True)

    full, cut = base / f"{a.name}.mp4", base / f"{a.name}-cut.mp4"
    render(full, segments(False))
    print("wrote", full, f"({duration(full):.0f}s)")
    render(cut, segments(True))
    print("wrote", cut, f"({duration(cut):.0f}s; waiting sped up {a.speed:g}x over {sum(t - f for f, t in waits):.0f}s)")

    lines = [f"Full-length file ({a.name}.mp4): time, what", ""]
    for c in sorted(data["cues"], key=lambda c: c.get("t") or c.get("from")):
        s = ((c.get("t") or c["from"]) - t0) / 1000
        what = {
            "vo": lambda c: f"voice-over: {c['key']} ({c['seconds']}s)",
            "page": lambda c: f"page {c['page']} shown (picture: {c['picture']})",
            "wait": lambda c: f"WAITING {(c['to'] - c['from']) / 1000:.0f}s {c.get('label', '')} (sped up in the cut)",
            "movie": lambda c: f"the real movie plays ({(c['to'] - c['from']) / 1000:.0f}s)",
        }[c["type"]](c)
        lines.append(f"{int(s // 60)}:{s % 60:04.1f}  {what}")
    (base / f"{a.name}-cues.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Build the demo videos from the recordings and the voice-over: the 3-minute pitch video and the full tour.

  python scripts/build_pitch_video.py pitch        # evidence/demo/storybound-demo-3min.mp4 (at most 3:00)
  python scripts/build_pitch_video.py tour         # evidence/full-tour/storybound-full-tour.mp4 (every feature, including the grown-up side)

Sources (screen recordings, silent unless noted): evidence/app-capture/app-walkthrough.mp4 (the app, with its own sound; its sound without the voice-over is
work/apponly.wav), the three dashboard recordings neatlogs.mp4, entire.mp4, cfo.ai.mp4 at the repo root, and evidence/features-capture/. The voice-over is
text-to-speech (scripts/make_demo_voiceover.py). Each scene is one voice-over line over one or more clips, with an optional caption; a scene lasts as long as
its voice-over (or its clips, if longer). Links on the end card come from evidence/demo/links.json (live, demo, code).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FFMPEG = "C:/ffmpeg/ffmpeg.exe"
FFPROBE = "C:/ffmpeg/ffprobe.exe"
FONT = "C\\:/Windows/Fonts/arialbd.ttf"
W, H = 1920, 1080

AC = ROOT / "evidence" / "app-capture"
FC = ROOT / "evidence" / "features-capture"
SRC = {"aw": AC / "app-walkthrough.mp4", "nl": ROOT / "neatlogs.mp4", "en": ROOT / "entire.mp4", "cf": ROOT / "cfo.ai.mp4"}


def dur(p: Path) -> float:
    o = subprocess.run([FFPROBE, "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return float(o.stdout.strip())


def part(src: str, start: float, d: float, speed: float = 1.0, audio: float = 0.0, file: Path | None = None, audio_file: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    return {"file": file or SRC[src], "start": start, "d": d, "speed": speed, "audio": audio, "audio_file": audio_file or (AC / "work" / "apponly.wav")}


def cap(text: str, a: float, b: float) -> tuple[str, float, float]:
    return (text, a, b)


def esc(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\u2019").replace(":", "\\:").replace("%", "\\%").replace(",", "\\,")


def build_scene(k: int, out: Path, vo: Path | None, parts: list[dict], captions: list, card: list[str] | None = None, min_d: float = 0.0, lead: float = 0.3) -> float:
    vo_d = dur(vo) if vo else 0.0
    clip_d = sum(p["d"] / p["speed"] for p in parts) if parts else 0.0
    D = max(clip_d, vo_d + lead + 0.5, min_d)
    ins: list[str] = []
    f: list[str] = []
    n = 0
    labels = []
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        ins += ["-ss", f"{p['start']:.3f}", "-t", f"{p['d']:.3f}", "-i", str(p["file"])]
        f.append(f"[{n}:v]setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/{p['speed']},scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad={W}:{H}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,fps=30,format=yuv420p,setsar=1[p{i}]")
        labels.append(f"[p{i}]")
        n += 1
    if parts:
        f.append(f"{''.join(labels)}concat=n={len(parts)}:v=1:a=0[vc]")
        pad = f",tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration={max(0.0, D - clip_d):.3f}" if D > clip_d + 0.01 else ""
        f.append(f"[vc]null{pad}[vb]")
    else:
        f.append(f"color=c=0x1b1a2e:s={W}x{H}:d={D:.3f}:r=30,format=yuv420p[vb]")
    cur = "vb"
    j = 0
    if card:
        y = 250
        for line, size in [(l.split("|")[0], int(l.split("|")[1]) if "|" in l else 54) for l in card]:
            f.append(f"[{cur}]drawtext=fontfile='{FONT}':text='{esc(line)}':fontsize={size}:fontcolor=white:x=(w-text_w)/2:y={y}[c{j}]")
            cur = f"c{j}"
            j += 1
            y += int(size * 1.9)
    for text, a, b in captions:
        f.append(f"[{cur}]drawtext=fontfile='{FONT}':text='{esc(text)}':fontsize=46:fontcolor=white:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.62:boxborderw=22:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=h-150:enable='between(t,{a:.2f},{b:.2f})'[c{j}]")
        cur = f"c{j}"
        j += 1
    f.append(f"[{cur}]null[v]")
    # audio: the voice-over (a little after the scene starts) and any real narration under it
    alabels = []
    if vo:
        ins += ["-i", str(vo)]
        f.append(f"[{n}:a]aformat=sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo,volume=1.3,adelay={int(lead * 1000)}|{int(lead * 1000)}[va]")
        alabels.append("[va]")
        n += 1
    off = 0.0
    for p in parts:
        if p["audio"] > 0:
            ins += ["-ss", f"{p['start']:.3f}", "-t", f"{p['d']:.3f}", "-i", str(p["audio_file"])]
            f.append(f"[{n}:a]aformat=sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo,volume={p['audio']},adelay={int(off * 1000)}|{int(off * 1000)}[ra{n}]")
            alabels.append(f"[ra{n}]")
            n += 1
        off += p["d"] / p["speed"]
    if alabels:
        f.append(f"{''.join(alabels)}amix=inputs={len(alabels)}:normalize=0:duration=longest,apad,atrim=0:{D:.3f}[a]")
    else:
        f.append(f"anullsrc=r=44100:cl=stereo,atrim=0:{D:.3f}[a]")
    gf = out.with_suffix(".graph.txt")
    gf.write_text(";\n".join(f), encoding="utf-8")
    subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", *ins, "-filter_complex_script", str(gf), "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]", "-t", f"{D:.3f}", "-r", "30", "-c:v", "libx264", "-crf", "20", "-preset", "veryfast", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "160k", "-ar", "44100", str(out)], check=True)
    return D


def concat(scenes: list[Path], out: Path) -> None:
    lst = out.with_suffix(".txt")
    lst.write_text("\n".join(f"file '{s.as_posix()}'" for s in scenes), encoding="utf-8")
    subprocess.run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-v", "error", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", str(lst), "-c", "copy", str(out)], check=True)


def cues(path: Path) -> dict:
    d = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    t0 = json.loads((path.parent / "frames.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))[0][0] if (path.parent / "frames.json").exists() else d["recStart"]
    vo = {c["key"]: (c["t"] - t0) / 1000 for c in d["cues"] if c["type"] == "vo"}
    page = {c["page"]: (c["t"] - t0) / 1000 for c in d["cues"] if c["type"] == "page"}
    waits = [((c["from"] - t0) / 1000, (c["to"] - t0) / 1000) for c in d["cues"] if c["type"] == "wait"]
    return {"vo": vo, "page": page, "waits": waits, "t0": t0}


def links() -> dict:
    p = ROOT / "evidence" / "demo" / "links.json"
    base = {"live": "<live app link>", "demo": "<demo link>", "code": "github.com/hatif03/storybound"}
    if p.exists():
        base.update(json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    return base


def pitch() -> None:
    work = ROOT / "evidence" / "pitch-video" / "work"
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    vdir = ROOT / "evidence" / "pitch-video" / "voiceover"
    c = cues(AC / "work" / "cues.json") if (AC / "work" / "cues.json").exists() else cues(AC / "recording-cues.json")
    wait_to = c["waits"][0][1]
    lk = links()
    scenes = [
        ("c1", [part("aw", c["vo"]["draw"] + 1, 18, 1.0)], [cap("27 of 28 AI-written stories broke a promise", 5.5, 16)], None),
        ("c2", [part("aw", c["vo"]["lesson"] - 3, 20, 1.0)], [cap("Promises first: a checkable oath for each drawing and lesson", 3, 20)], None),
        ("c3", [part("aw", wait_to - 60, 16, 1.0)], [cap("Every page is checked before the child sees it", 2, 16)], None),
        ("c4", [part("aw", c["page"][1] - 0.3, 22, 1.0, audio=0.45)], [cap("It reads itself aloud, with a replay button", 2, 12), cap("Kind choices and a verified quiz", 12, 22)], None),
        ("c5", [part("aw", c["vo"]["receipt"] - 0.5, 15, 1.0)], [cap("The receipt: nothing hidden. 0 of 28 shipped a broken promise", 2, 15)], None),
        ("c6", [part("nl", 22, 12, 1.0)], [cap("neatlogs: one trace per story, every promise a quoted verdict", 1, 11)], None),
        ("c7", [part("nl", 66, 24, 1.0), part("nl", 94, 8, 1.0)], [cap("Writer broke the page format: 3 of 10 failed, then 10 of 10", 1, 10), cap("Judge down: 0 of 5 shipped, with a second judge 5 of 5", 10, 18.5), cap("Repair loop never ends? No: our tracing lost spans. Fixed.", 18.5, 31)], None),
        ("c9", [part("en", 8, 6, 1.0), part("en", 16, 7, 1.0), part("en", 30, 5, 1.0)], [cap("Entire: one checkpoint per fix, a review, runners that gate the next change", 1, 17)], None),
        ("c10", [part("cf", 5, 11, 1.0), part("cf", 26, 7, 1.0)], [cap("cfo.ai: the cost of a story became a product decision", 1, 18)], None),
        ("c11", [], [], ["Storybound|96", "Promises first. Checked before the child sees a page.|46", "A receipt for the parent.|46", f"Live app: {lk['live']}|40", f"Free demo: {lk['demo']}|40", f"Code: {lk['code']}|40", "#neatHack  @neatlogs  @EntireHQ  @arithecfo|36"]),
    ]
    out_scenes, total = [], 0.0
    for k, (vid, parts, caps, card) in enumerate(scenes):
        out = work / f"scene{k:02d}.mp4"
        d = build_scene(k, out, vdir / f"{vid}.mp3", parts, caps, card, min_d=(11.0 if vid == "c11" else 0.0))
        total += d
        out_scenes.append(out)
        print(f"{vid}: {d:.1f}s (total {total:.1f}s)", flush=True)
    final = ROOT / "evidence" / "demo" / "storybound-demo-3min.mp4"
    final.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    concat(out_scenes, final)
    print("wrote", final, f"{dur(final):.1f}s")
    if dur(final) > 180:
        sys.exit(f"too long: {dur(final):.1f}s")


def tour() -> None:
    sys.exit("tour: built by scripts/build_pitch_video.py after the feature recording; see build_tour() once the recording exists")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    {"pitch": pitch, "tour": tour}[sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "pitch"]()

Both recordings and the deployment are running in the background. The merge is done, and the README now opens with the problem and solution in plain language, with a new [docs/WHY.md](docs/WHY.md) on who it helps.

**Status**
- **PR 4 is merged into `main`.**
  - Its Entire gate showed two findings on the way: chaos injection could be switched on by a stray environment setting, and the new autoplay. I fixed the first so it now needs a named drill to run, and recorded the second as a deliberate rule.
  - The solo "approvals" gate stays unmet.
- **Public deployment:** the AWS agent is building it with small daily caps and tracing turned off. The caps are 40 stories a day, 3 per visitor, and 8 movies. The free demo link (`/?mock=1`) has no limit. The README links are placeholders until it reports back.
- **Recordings, both running now:**
  - The main app capture is being redone because the last one never showed the receipt, since the screen recorder skipped that static screen. It now takes a frame every second, so none can be missed.
  - A feature tour is being recorded for the full-length video. It covers the grown-up gate, every setting, About, a refused drawing, writing inside a drawing that gets ignored, start over and bring-it-back, a real story, the movie, the receipt and Forget.
- **Your dashboard clips:** they are silent, so I'm adding voice-over to them. I'm skipping the Entire session segment at 36–40 s, because it shows a message about the leaked key.
- **Videos:** a builder script is ready for the 3-minute pitch video (about 150 seconds of voice-over) and the full tour. Once the recordings finish I'll build them and fill in the README links.

  - The code is cloned at `/opt/storybound` (commit 7f8e97d) into a venv. The built `web/dist` was rebuilt locally and copied up.
  - The app runs as user `storybound` under `storybound.service` on port 80, with a read-only checkout except `runs/`.

result.output:
The judges page has these sections, in order:

1. **Title and quick links:** "neatHack 2026, for judges" with judge names, a film link, jump links, and a note that receipts were re-issued Oct 11. A weighted list of the five criteria (30/25/20/15/10%) follows.
2. **Behind Every Run:** A tool-logo row, a neatlogs screenshot, then one block per tool (neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai). Each block has a screenshot, a headline, three numbered stats, and link buttons.
3. **All 7 Official Evidence Rows:** A numbered list. Each row has a tag (In repo, Screenshots, Public), a one-line description, and a link.
4. **The Agent Runs a Quickstart:** A v1-vs-v2 comparison with deltas, a recovery trace as numbered steps, a "Show details" panel with code links, and a six-metric table.
5. **neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai:** Three subsections with the richest evidence:
   - **neatlogs:** Stat callouts, a link to the evidence file, and a grid of ten captioned screenshots (N1–N10). A note explains that trace pages need a login, so screenshots stand in.
   - **Entire:** Three stats, a link to a checkpoint commit, a count breakdown, six captioned screenshots (E1–E6), and terminal-output blocks showing git log and graph output.
   - **cfo.ai:** Three stats, a link to the public model, Free/Team/Scale plan cards (price, cap, margin), a cash-on-hand chart with a caption, a scenario table, five captioned screenshots (C1–C5), and a "Show details" panel.
6. **Demo video:** A film embed with timestamped chapter links and a table of per-tool chapters.
7. **Built in public:** A timeline of 11 posts tagged #neatHack, with a clickable list.
8. **Upstream PRs:** Four numbered PRs (P1–P4) with links, plus summary stats and receipt links.
9. **Five things that broke:** A numbered list of problems, each with a number.
10. **Verify from your terminal:** Copy-ready command blocks with expected outputs.
11. **Footer:** Site navigation and credits.

**Short answers:** Each section opens with bold headline numbers and one-line facts, such as "52.8x spike" or "91 of 132 commits." These serve as the page's quick answers, and the "Show details" panels hold the longer explanations.

result.output:
## 2. Entire

### Architecture
Entire records the *coding agent*. CLI 0.11.4 with hooks installed for Claude Code, `commit_linking: always`, checkpoints synced to `origin`. Each commit made in a repo-rooted session gets an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer; the checkpoint holds the session transcript, files and token use. `entire-graph` 0.4.0 (local, no network) and Entire Brain 0.1.0 (installed from the release, refreshed on a clean tree) add structural and memory views.

### Implementation
- One commit per intent so each checkpoint maps to one change. 40 or more checkpoints at the time of writing (`entire checkpoint list`). Every hardening record names the commit and its checkpoint id.
- **Graph evidence** (`evidence/entire/`): `graph diff` for the HR-001, HR-002, HR-003, HR-004 and HR-006 changes (the entities each fix touched), `graph impact` for `verify_scene_async` and `story_safe_text`, `graph verify` before and after.
- **`entire why`** on `src/storybound/oath/catalog.py` ties 18 lines to the checkpoint of the `image_no_text` change; on `pipeline.py` it ties lines to the HR-002 ablation switch.
- **Brain:** ten durable facts, among them "video specs never hold typed numbers", "a failure not tied to a scene stops the repair loop", and "a key pasted into a chat is recorded in checkpoint transcripts"; `brain brief` returns the likely files for a task.
- **`checkpoint tokens --compare`** between two checkpoints (`evidence/entire/20261010-1955-IST-checkpoint-tokens-HR-006-vs-HR-001-test.txt`); the tool itself warns that cache replay dominates the totals.

### Runtime and reasoning
The checkpoints are how a reader answers "why is this prompt this way": the HR commit messages carry the trigger, the trace ids and the before/after numbers, and the checkpoint carries the session that wrote them.

### Trails (two trails; trail 2 is backed by a branch and a PR)
- `entire runner setup --defaults-only` created the six trail runners (risk, confidence, drift, review, security, summary) with no model call. The **security, drift and review runners are tailored to this repo's hard rules** (no secrets, no child data, evidence discipline, the oath as the product, no timers or streaks for children) and committed under `.entire/runners/`.
- First attempt (before the builder enabled Trails on the dashboard): `entire trail create` and `entire review general` answered **"repository not found (404)"**.
- After Trails, Runners and Auto build were switched on in entire.io: `entire trail create --repo gh/hatif03/storybound --no-branch --title ... --type feature` **worked**. Trail **#1, ID `01M4MG92JRX974RCWS1FQ1ZWJ8`**, https://entire.io/gh/hatif03/storybound/trails/1 (evidence: `evidence/entire/20261011-0925-IST-trail-1-created.txt`). Per hack.entire.io section 06, each trail is backed by a GitHub PR and runners fire on push. The push was held back on purpose until the pasted keys were scrubbed from history (the permission check refused the first attempt and we did not work around it); the builder then approved a history rewrite, it was done on 11 Oct ([evidence/history-rewrite/NOTE.md](../evidence/history-rewrite/NOTE.md)), and the branch push went through.
- **Trail 2** (`01M4MK1J1NJYW4A4ZJ1DRQZEKD`, https://entire.io/gh/hatif03/storybound/trails/2) is backed by branch `docs/after-history-rewrite` and PR #1 on GitHub (the PR appeared by itself when the branch was pushed; checks: Entire Gates, GitGuardian Security Checks passed). `entire review general` ran on the branch against `main` with Claude Code: verdict "approve with nits", five findings (a real bug in `scripts/build_evidence.py` that printed the latest commit as the "First commit"; a missing exception for the approved rewrite in CLAUDE.md rule 1; stale Trails wording; a visibility wording gap; a missing PR reference). All five were fixed in the next commit. Gates on the trail (`evidence/entire/20261011-1030-IST-trail-2-gates.json`): checks passed (GitGuardian), up to date passed, **approvals failed** (the trail's rule wants one reviewer and does not allow self-approval, and this is

### Result and limits (said plainly)
- Early work (the first ~13:00 to 14:30 IST of Saturday, M1 to M5 and the first sweeps) was done in a session started outside the repository, so it has **no checkpoint**; the HR-001 and HR-002 *change* commits (`04ffebb`, `daec9ea`) say so. `entire why` shows most older code as "human" for the same reason.
- **Keys in checkpoints, and the fix.** Two keys were pasted into the session (a neatlogs key and the hackathon gateway key). Entire had already masked the neatlogs key as `REDACTED`; the gateway key was in the text of three transcript files across many checkpoint-ref commits. Entire documents no way to remove a pushed checkpoint, so on 11 Oct, with the builder's approval, the history was rewritten with `git filter-repo` (key text replaced on every ref including `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`; the sister's drawings removed from every commit), and the rewritten refs were force-pushed one by one to the private `origin`. A fresh clone of the remote was scanned: 0 files contain any key value, 0 commits touch the removed images; `entire checkpoint list` and `explain` still resolve (checkpoint ids are not shas). New checkpoints now mask key shapes through `redaction.custom_redactions` in `.entire
- The checkpoint link the submission needs is `https://entire.io/gh/hatif03/storybound/commit/<FULL_SHA>` plus the 26-character checkpoint id from the commit trailer. The repository was made public on 11 Oct after the rewrite. Anonymous check (clean headless browser): `https://entire.io/gh/hatif03/storybound/commit/1a96c19fd6f99c981f7e6b7cbbea715d25eb55d2` rendered the commit page with its checkpoint trailer `01M4MJM5TRM7NE2F8FHFJ49NE6` (`evidence/screens/20261011-1015-IST-entire-commit-link-anonymous.png`); a Log in button is visible but not required to read it.
- `brain refresh` refuses a dirty working tree (found by running it); `entire checkpoint explain --generate`, `entire dispatch` and `entire import` were not run (they spend model tokens or add pre-window history).

---

## 3. cfo.ai

### Reasoning: how traces led to fixes
Our rule is trace first (`CLAUDE.md`): find the failure in neatlogs, write the hypothesis, fix, compare runs. What that produced:

| Record | What the trace showed | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [HR-001](../evidence/hardening/HR-001.md) | Reading level broke on most first-pass pages (trace `264208295ada9b28a96d2e29b32fb41c`, 7 repairs) | Writer told the limit: B0 pages over the limit 42.9% to 1.8% |
| [HR-002](../evidence/hardening/HR-002.md) | Review made gated stories slow | Pipelined review: total time -35% (mean) in a same-jobs ablation; time to first page did **not** improve, and the record says so |

← Back to the app

Storybound, for the neatHack judges

A bedtime-story helper that checks its own work, so a parent doesn't have to. A child draws a hero; before any page reaches the child, the agent has checked it against promises it wrote first, rewritten what broke, and afterwards it hands the parent a receipt.

Open the live app Free demo mode 3-minute video Full tour video Code

The problemHow we used the toolsneatlogsEntirecfo.aiWhat the tools changedWhat brokeVerify it yourself

The problem and the solution

Problem. AI can write a story about your child's drawing in seconds, and nobody checks it. In our own experiment the same writer, left alone, slipped at least one broken promise into 27 of 28 stories (a lesson that never showed up, the right answer always in the same place, words too hard for the age, sometimes an unkind line). A parent cannot read every story first.

Solution. The agent writes an oath (a checkable list of promises) for each drawing and lesson, checks every page against it with simple rules and an independent second AI, rewrites any page that breaks a promise, shows a page only when its words, picture and voice all exist, and gives the parent a receipt. With every page checked, 0 of 28 stories shipped a broken promise. Why it matters to families and communities: docs/WHY.md.

What the judges score: the agent 30%, use of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai 25%, demo video 20%, building in public 15%, usefulness and originality 10%. The page below is the 25%.

How we used the tools

1 traceper story in neatlogs; every promise is one quoted verdict span
97 checkpointsin Entire, one per change; 4 trails merged, each with runners and a review
67.8% vs 43.4%margin the cfo.ai model gave for painting half the pages versus all of them

Short answers to the three questions of the submission form follow, each with evidence links and screenshots from our own dashboards. Trace and trail pages need a login, so the screenshots stand in for them; the repository holds exported traces and the files behind every number.

We then used neatlogs to find our own bugs: its incidents, detections, alerts, error spans and evaluations led to nine fixes with before and after numbers. Trace first, then fix, was our written rule (CLAUDE.md).

7,100+traces from our runs, sweeps, drills and experiments (dashboard home: 7,123 sessions in 7 days)
4 resolvedincident cards, each checked against the trace and closed with a note
10 detections, 7 alertsincluding a picture-words detection that fired on a drill, and email delivery

Entire: how did you use it?

Short answer

Entire recorded the coding agent that built Storybound. We made one commit per intent so each checkpoint maps to one change, used entire-graph to see what a change touched before and after, used Trails with tailored runners and entire review to gate each pull request, and recorded durable decisions in Brain. Its reviews found real defects in our own work, which we fixed.

Short answer

cfo.ai turned "what does a story cost?" into product decisions. Painting every page leaves a 43% gross margin against our 60% bar, painting half clears it at 67%, so the agent now spends a fixed picture budget on the pages that matter most. We replaced the cost estimate with the cost neatlogs measured, it showed that video AI would take the margin to minus 70%, so video is left out, and it priced what a real launch needs (about 2,490 paying households at $6.99).

I've built the judges evidence section in the same style as the example you linked, and added the form answers to the README and the submission checklist. The page isn't live yet, because the deployment needs the next build. The main app recording is still running, and the feature-tour recording has to be redone sequentially after it.

**Judges page** (`web/public/judges/index.html`, served at `<live app>/judges/`):
- It covers the problem and solution, then one section per tool, each opening with the form's own question and a short answer.
- Each tool has stat boxes, a table of what it showed us and what we changed, and links to the repo files behind every claim.
- The screenshots you added are in as 21 compressed images with captions: neatlogs N1–N7, Entire E1–E7, cfo.ai C1–C7. They are also filed under `evidence/dashboards/` in the repo.
- Below that it has "recommendations from the tools and what we changed", "what broke", and "verify it yourself". The app's About tab now links to it.

**Entire "open-source builds":** we didn't contribute code to Entire's own repositories, and the page says so. It lists what we built on top: six tailored trail runners, custom key redactions, Claude Code with commit linking, and the evidence scripts.

**README and submission:** the README now opens with the plain-language problem and solution, a "Try it" table, and the three form answers with links. The same answers are in [docs/SUBMISSION.md](docs/SUBMISSION.md) for copy and paste. Live-app and video links are placeholders until the deployment is final.

**Deployment:** the demo server is up, but real stories fail there for lack of Google credentials. Google's organisation policy refused to create a service-account key, and I did not override that policy. I've asked the deployment agent to set up keyless access instead (Workload Identity Federation), restricted to the server's own AWS role. It is still working on that.

I've also added a note on the draw screen and in About asking people not to upload a photo of a real child. The deployed copy needs a redeploy to pick that up.
